definition_zh: 预告片；先看；预览；预展；预演
definition_en: a chance to see something before the public sees it, or to see it before it is finished
core_image: 幕布只拉开一道缝，观众先看一眼正片
scene: 影院灯暗下之后，先放了一段新片的片段。Before the film began, the cinema showed a two minute preview of next month releases.
sceneCN: 这里 preview 是「预告片」（第 1 个义项：在片子正式推出之前先让人看的一小段）；句意：影院灯暗下之后，先放了一段新片的片段。

pos.zh: 预先观看；预展；为……举行预演

collocations.phrase: a preview of the new season

derivatives.zh: -er 后缀：先观看者；预览程序
同根名词：观看者、观众
另一前缀的同根词：再观看，因此指评论或复审
同根名词：景象；视野；看法

senses.title: A trailer before the film
senses.definition: a short advertisement showing clips from a film that is not out yet
senses.definitionCN: 展示尚未上映影片片段的短视频广告
senses.example: The preview for the documentary lasted ninety seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 那部纪录片的预告片长达九十秒。
senses.why: Pre- puts the seeing in front of the event, so a preview is a first look given before the whole thing arrives.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 pre- 把「看」放在事件之前，所以 preview 是整件事到来之前先给的一眼。

senses.title: A viewing before the public
senses.definition: an event at which a small group sees a work before ordinary viewers do
senses.definitionCN: 在普通观众之前让一小群人参看作品的场合
senses.example: Critics crowded into the preview on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 影评人挤满了周一的试映场。
senses.why: When the first look is organised for guests or critics, the preview becomes an event with a door and a guest list.
senses.whyCN: 当「先看」是专门给客人或影评人安排的，preview 就成了一场有门和请柬的活动。

senses.title: A look on screen
senses.definition: a small or temporary display showing how a page or file will look
senses.definitionCN: 显示页面或文件最终样子的小窗或临时画面
senses.example: Check the preview before you send the file.
senses.exampleCN: 发送文件之前先检查一下预览。
senses.why: Software borrowed the old idea of seeing it first, giving it to the little window that shows the page before it is printed.
senses.whyCN: 软件借用了「先看一眼」的旧意，把它给了那个在打印之前显示页面样子的小窗口。

senses.title: To view beforehand
senses.definition: to watch or show something in advance of the usual time
senses.definitionCN: 在通常的时间之前观看或展示某物
senses.example: Journalists previewed the exhibition on Thursday.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们在周四预先参观了这场展览。
senses.why: The noun was easily turned into a verb, so anyone who views before the public can simply be said to preview the show.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词很容易转化成动词，因此任何人只要先于公众去看，就可以说成 preview 这场展览。

senses.title: A quick sketch of what is coming
senses.definition: a short account given in advance of what will follow in detail
senses.definitionCN: 在详细内容之前给出的简短说明
senses.example: The first chapter is a preview of the book argument.
senses.exampleCN: 第一章是对全书论点的预先概述。
senses.why: Any early glimpse works as a promise of the whole, so a short chapter or a season opener becomes a preview too.
senses.whyCN: 任何早期的一瞥都是对整体的预告，所以短短的一章或一季的开场集也成了 preview。

intro.en: Preview joins the Latin prefix prae- with the English word view, whose root is Latin videre, to see.
intro.cn: preview 由拉丁前缀 prae-「在前」与英语单词 view 组合而成，view 的词根是拉丁语 videre（看见）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visus gives the root vid- in vision and video.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，其过去分词 visus 给出 vid- 这个词根，vision 与 video 都来自它。

items.en: Old French veue named the act of seeing and the sight itself, and it came from the Latin past participle.
items.cn: 古法语 veue 既指「看」这个动作，也指眼前的景象，源自拉丁语过去分词。

items.en: English borrowed it as vewe and later spelled it view, widening from sight to the scene and to an opinion.
items.cn: 英语借入作 vewe，后拼作 view，词义从「看见」扩展到景象与看法。

items.en: The Latin prefix prae- meant before or in front, and English keeps it productive in words such as predict.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，英语在 predict 等词里一直沿用它。

items.en: English joined prae- to view as pre-view, the noun first meaning a seeing beforehand, from which the verb came.
items.cn: 英语把 prae- 与 view 拼成 preview，名词先表示「事先看」，动词随后从它派生。

items.en: Films, exhibitions, and software each gave the word a fresh use, from the trailer to the little window on a screen.
items.cn: 电影、展览与软件各自给它添了新用法，从预告片一直到屏幕上的小窗口。

note.en: Preview is the twin of review, differing only in a prefix, so it sits near review by form, and near trailer, trailer clip, and sneak peek by meaning.
note.cn: preview 与 review 只差一个前缀，形式上相邻；意义上靠近 trailer、trailer clip 与 sneak peek。

entries.definition: a critical report on a work, or a fresh look at it
entries.definitionCN: 评论；复审，与 preview 只差一个前缀

entries.definition: a person who views something
a formal meeting in which questions are put to someone
entries.definitionCN: 面试；采访，同样含 view 这一成分

entries.definition: a short clip advertising a film not yet released
entries.definitionCN: 电影预告片，比 preview 更强调广告性质

entries.definition: an early showing or sale, as in an advance screening
entries.definitionCN: 先行放映或预售，常与 screening 连用

entries.definition: a quick secret look at something
entries.definitionCN: 偷偷看一眼，如 sneak peek

normalIntro.en: Preview is simply pre- plus view, so it means seeing something before its proper time.
normalIntro.cn: preview 就是 pre- 加 view，字面意思是在该看的时候之前先看。

normal.en: The prefix pre- means before, as it does in predict and prepare.
normal.cn: 前缀 pre- 意为「在前」，predict 与 prepare 里的 pre- 也是这个意思。

normal.en: The root vid- means to see, and it survives in video and vision.
normal.cn: 词根 vid- 意为「看见」，video 与 vision 里还可以看到它。

normal.en: Compare review: review looks back, preview looks ahead.
normal.cn: 对比 review：review 是回头看，preview 是往前看。

normal.en: A sneak preview is a showing before anyone else is allowed in.
normal.cn: a sneak preview 是在别人获准进场之前偷偷放的场次。

normal.en: Software print preview shows the page before the printer gets it.
normal.cn: 软件的 print preview 在打印之前先显示页面的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain pulled back a hand width for one early pair of eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布只被拉开一掌宽，只给最先到场的一双眼睛看。

abstract.en: Picture a few dozen people in an empty cinema, a week early.
abstract.cn: 想象几十个人提前一周坐在空荡荡的影院里。

abstract.en: Picture a page shown small on a screen, printed only after you nod.
abstract.cn: 想象页面先小样似的出现在屏幕上，你点头之后才真正打印。

examples.en: The studio released a preview of the sequel last week.
examples.cn: 制片厂上周发布了续集的预告片。

examples.en: Guests previewed the exhibition before it opened to the public.
examples.cn: 宾客们在展览对公众开放前先参观了预展。

examples.en: She switched to preview mode to check the layout.
examples.cn: 她切换到预览模式检查版面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞view」——先说一声「普瑞」，让大家提前看一眼；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ 过去分词 visus → 古法语 veue → 英语 view；再加拉丁前缀 prae-、英语拼作 pre- → preview，核心义「在正式对外之前先看一眼」。

sensesIntro.en: Preview starts with the film trailer, then the private showing, then the small on screen look, then the verb, and finally any early glimpse that hints at what follows.
sensesIntro.cn: preview 从电影预告片开始，再到内部试映、屏幕上小窗式的预览，接着转成动词，最后泛指任何预示后续的提前一瞥。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain pulled back a hand width before the show begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：开演之前，幕布被拉开一掌宽的缝。

branches.en: The trailer is the commonest modern sense.
branches.cn: 预告片是现代最常见的义项。

branches.en: A showing for invited guests is the social sense.
branches.cn: 给受邀客人安排的放映或预展是社会义项。

branches.en: The screen preview and the verb carry the same look into software and into action.
branches.cn: 屏幕预览把这个「看一眼」带进软件，动词形式则把它变成动作。

branches.en: A trailer and a press screening both let people see the film early.
branches.cn: 预告片与媒体试映都是让人们提前看到片子。

branches.en: A print preview and a first chapter both show a small version of a larger whole.
branches.cn: 打印预览与第一章都是一个更大整体的缩小版。

intro.en: Preview pairs the Latin prefix prae- with the English word view, whose vowel and spelling come from the French descendant of Latin videre.
intro.cn: preview 把拉丁前缀 prae- 与英语单词 view 配在一起，view 的读音与拼写传承自拉丁语 videre 的法语后代。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre means to see, and prae- means in front, so preview is a seeing placed in front of the main event.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 意为「看见」，prae- 意为「在前」，所以 preview 就是放在主事件之前的一次观看。

items.example: The prefix prae- sets the looking before the event.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 把观看放到事件之前。

items.example: Videre is the deepest root of the word.
items.exampleCN: videre 是这个词最深的词根。

items.example: The root vid- appears in video and vision.
items.exampleCN: 词根 vid- 出现在 video 与 vision 里。

items.example: The participle visus reaches English in vision and visual.
items.exampleCN: 过去分词 visus 以 vision 与 visual 的形式进入英语。

items.meaning: a sight, or the act of seeing
items.example: View is the English half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: view 是这个合成词的英语一半。

items.example: The prefix pre- also shapes predict and prepare.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 也构成 predict 与 prepare。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does
items.example: The suffix -er forms previewer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 previewer。

items.meaning: a look back, a critical report
items.example: Review shares the view but reverses the prefix.
items.exampleCN: review 共享 view 这一部分，但前缀相反。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词的词尾
items.example: The ending -ed forms previewed.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 previewed。

items.example: The ending -ing forms previewing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 previewing。

definition_zh: 太古的；原始太古时代的；远古的；原始的；未经开化的
definition_en: of or belonging to the earliest ages of the earth and of life, before history and civilisation
core_image: 薄雾笼罩的原始森林，树冠遮天，藤蔓垂落，脚下是从未被开垦过的泥地
scene: 纪录片的开头拍着一片从未被砍伐的雨林，树高得望不到顶。The film opens on a primeval forest where no tree has ever been cut.
sceneCN: 这里 primeval 是「以太古时代的原始状态为主的」（第 1 个义项：属于地壳与生命最早时期的事物）；句意：纪录片开头出现在一片原始森林里，那里从未有树被砍伐。

pos.zh: 太古的；原始太古时代的；远古的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「原始地；太古地」
同以「时代」概念构成，前缀为表示「之前」的 pre-，义为「史前时期」

senses.title: Dating from the earliest ages of the earth
senses.titleCN: 太古的；地壳最早期形成的
senses.definition: formed in or belonging to the most ancient period of the earth, long before human history
senses.definitionCN: 在地球最古老时期形成或属于那个时期的，远在人类历史之前
senses.example: Geologists study these primeval rocks for clues about the early earth.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家研究这些太古岩石，以寻找早期地球的线索。
senses.why: The first age of anything is its prime in the old sense, so primeval names whatever comes from that beginning.
senses.whyCN: 任何事物的最初时期在古义上就是它的「第一」，所以 primeval 指从那个开端留下的一切；核心意象里从未被砍伐的森林正是这种「第一时期」的标本。

senses.title: Unchanged since the earliest times
senses.titleCN: 原始状态的；未经人改动的
senses.definition: remaining in its original condition, untouched by human development
senses.definitionCN: 保持原先状态、未受人类开发影响的
senses.example: A primeval forest still holds trees that have stood for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 一片原始森林里仍有矗立了数百年的树木。
senses.why: If a place still looks as it did in the first age, the same word fits its present condition.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个地方如今仍像第一个时期那样，同一个词就自然用来形容它眼下的状态：森林虽在今日，却仍是「太古的样子」。

senses.title: Instinctive or rough, like an early ancestor
senses.definition: simple, instinctive, or rough in a way thought typical of early humans
senses.definitionCN: 简单、本能或粗野的，被认为像早期人类的典型样子
senses.example: Fear of the dark is a primeval instinct we share with other animals.
senses.exampleCN: 怕黑是我们与其他动物共有的原始本能。
senses.why: The earliest age still sits inside the mind, so a feeling that seems older than reason is called primeval.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的时期仍留在人的头脑里，于是那种比理智更早、更深的情绪就被称作「原始的」；核心意象从外部森林转向人内心的密林。

senses.title: Belonging to a time before civilisation
senses.titleCN: 远古的；文明形成之前的
senses.definition: belonging to or recalling the long age before cities, law, and writing appeared
senses.definitionCN: 属于或令人想起城市、法律与文字出现之前那漫长年代的
senses.example: The huts looked primeval beside the modern glass towers.
senses.exampleCN: 那些茅屋矗立在现代玻璃大楼旁，看上去十分远古。
senses.why: From earth history the word slides into human history, marking the stretch before civilisation.
senses.whyCN: 从地球史滑向人类史，这个词便用来标记文明出现之前那段漫长的岁月；这种推移来自核心意象中「时间上最早」这一要点。

senses.title: Wild and little changed by people
senses.definition: describing a landscape that is wild, remote, and almost untouched by people
senses.definitionCN: 形容风景荒凉、偏远、几乎没有人迹的
senses.example: The river cut through a primeval valley where no road had ever been built.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河穿过一个荒古的山谷，那里从未修过一条路。
senses.why: A place that looks untouched can be described as if it had come out of the first age.
senses.whyCN: 一处看起来没人动过的地方，就可以被描写成像从第一个时期直接走出来的一样；这种用法把「太古」从时间标签变成了风景描写。

intro.en: Primeval is formed in English from Latin primus, first, and aevum, age, parallel to such words as medieval.
intro.cn: primeval 是英语在拉丁要素基础上构成的词，由 primus（第一）与 aevum（时代）组成，与 medieval 等词结构平行。

items.en: Primus means first, and aevum means age or lifetime.
items.cn: primus 意为第一，aevum 意为时代或一生。

items.en: Scholastic Latin uses primaevus, of the first age, for what is earliest.
items.cn: 中世纪经院拉丁语用形容词 primaevus 表示「第一时期的，最早的」。

items.en: Seventeenth-century English writers coin primeval for the earliest ages of the world.
items.cn: 十七世纪的英语作者造出 primeval，用来指世界最古老的各个时期。

items.en: Natural historians apply it to fossils, rocks, and forests that seemed to date from the earth first age.
items.cn: 博物学家把它用于化石、岩石与森林，因为它们仿佛来自地球的第一个时期。

items.en: Modern usage extends it to instincts, valleys, and any condition felt to be untouched by civilisation.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到本能、山谷，以及任何被认为未被文明触及的状态。

note.en: Primeval sits in a busy family of prim- words and overlaps with words for the earliest age and for what is wild.
note.cn: primeval 身处庞大的 prim- 词族，同时与「最早时期」和「荒野未改」这两类词意义相叠。

entries.definition: belonging to the earliest stage of development
entries.definitionCN: 原始的；早期发展阶段的

entries.definition: first in rank or the best time of life
first in importance or in order of existence
belonging to the distant past
in its original, unspoiled condition
belonging to the time before written records

normalIntro.en: Primeval is simply first plus age: prim tells you it is the first thing, and the rest of the word is the long stretch of time it belongs to.
normalIntro.cn: primeval 其实就是「第一」加「时代」：prim 说明它是第一个，其余部分说明它属于哪一段漫长的时间。

normal.en: Prime in this word is the Latin primus, first, as in prime and primary.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 prime 是拉丁语 primus（第一），与 prime、primary 同源。

normal.en: The ending echoes medieval, which is the middle age, so primeval is the first age.
normal.cn: 词尾与 medieval（中世纪）呼应，medieval 是中间的时代，primeval 就是第一个时代。

normal.en: A primeval forest is one that has never been cut, unlike a planted plantation.
normal.cn: primeval forest 指从未被砍伐的森林，与人工林不同。

normal.en: Primeval rocks and primeval ooze belong to geology, the oldest layers of the earth.
normal.cn: primeval rocks 与 primeval ooze 都属于地质学，指地球最古老的层次。

normal.en: Compare primitive, which stresses a simple early stage, while primeval stresses great age.
normal.cn: 对比 primitive：primitive 强调简单的早期阶段，primeval 强调年代的久远。

abstract.en: Picture a fine mist over soil that no foot has yet pressed.
abstract.cn: 想象一层薄雾笼在还没有任何脚印踩过的泥土上方。

abstract.en: Think of an old tree whose rings reach back to the first age of the world.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵老树，年轮一直追溯回世界的第一个时期。

abstract.en: Feel a sudden fright in the dark, older than any reason you can name.
abstract.cn: 感受黑暗里突如其来的一惊，那种恐惧比你叫得出名字的任何道理都更古老。

examples.en: The expedition crossed a primeval marsh that few people had ever visited.
examples.cn: 探险队穿过一片几乎无人到访的原始沼泽。

examples.en: Scientists found primeval bacteria living deep beneath the sea floor.
examples.cn: 科学家在海底深处发现了太古细菌。

examples.en: The painting suggests a primeval world of fog, rock, and cold water.
examples.cn: 这幅画呈现出由雾、岩石与冷水构成的远古世界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普赖密我」——天气再「密」，也盖不住那片最为古老的森林；把「密」想成遮天的树冠，就联想到了 primeval。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 primus（第一）＋ aevum（时代）→ 中世纪拉丁语 primaevus（第一时期的）→ 英语 primeval（太古的），核心义「属于第一个时代」。

sensesIntro.en: Primeval begins with the earliest age of the earth, then applies that age to places still in their original state, to instincts felt as older than reason, to life before civilisation, and to any wild landscape.
sensesIntro.cn: primeval 从地球最早期讲起，随后把这个「第一个时代」用到仍保持原状的地方、深于理智的本能、文明出现之前的生活，以及任何荒野风景上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a misty untouched forest older than any road or record.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片薄雾笼罩、从未被道路或文字触及的古老森林。

branches.en: The geological date of the earth first ages is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 地球最早时期的地质年代是这个词的本义。

branches.en: A place still in its first state takes the same label for its present looks.
branches.cn: 一个仍停留在最初状态的地方，就用同一个标签形容它眼下的样子。

branches.en: Old instincts keep the same age inside human feeling.
branches.cn: 古老的本能把这个时代带进了人的情感深处。

branches.en: The word then moves from earth history to the age before civilisation.
branches.cn: 接着这个词从地球史转向文明形成之前的人类岁月。

branches.en: A primeval forest is wild because it is untouched, so the two landscape senses nearly meld.
branches.cn: 原始森林之所以荒古，正因为它未被触动，所以这两种风景义项几乎合成一体。

intro.en: Primeval is built from the Latin root prim, first, and the age word aevum, with English relatives such as prime, primary, and primitive.
intro.cn: primeval 由拉丁词根 prim（第一）与表示时代的 aevum 构成，英语中的 prime、primary、primitive 是同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus means first, and aevum means age, so the Latin adjective primaevus means of the first age.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus 意为第一，aevum 意为时代，因此拉丁语形容词 primaevus 意为「第一时期的」。

items.example: The root marks what comes before everything else.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根标记在一切之前出现的东西。

items.example: Primus is the source of the first half of the word.
items.exampleCN: primus 是这个词前半部分的来源。

items.example: Aevum supplies the long age inside primeval.
items.exampleCN: aevum 为 primeval 提供了「漫长时代」的含义。

items.example: Primaevus is the Latin model behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: primaevus 是这个词背后的拉丁语原型。

items.example: Prime keeps the first in rank sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: prime 保留词根「居于第一」的含义。

items.example: Primitive stresses the early stage rather than the great age.
items.exampleCN: primitive 强调早期阶段而不是年代的久远。

items.example: Primal describes what lies at the very base of something.
items.exampleCN: primal 描述处于最底层的东西。

items.example: The ending -val also appears in medieval.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -val 也出现在 medieval 中。

items.example: Medieval pairs middle with age, as primeval pairs first with age.
items.exampleCN: medieval 是「中间」加「时代」，正如 primeval 是「第一」加「时代」。

definition_zh: 太古的；自原始存在的；最初始的；根本的；原基的
definition_en: existing from the very beginning, especially from the first formation of the earth or of an organism
core_image: 一锅翻滚的原始热汤，气泡自底部升起，那是最早的生命将要出现的地方
scene: 化学实验室的屏幕上，一个模型从一团混沌里慢慢浮出最初的轮廓。On the screen a model slowly takes its primordial shape out of the swirling broth.
sceneCN: 这里 primordial 是「最初始的、最早的形态的」（第 1 个义项：自最初就存在的）；句意：屏幕上的模型从翻滚的汤液中慢慢显出最初的轮廓。

collocations.zh: 原始汤；生命起源时代的溶液
根本需要；与生俱来的需求

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「原始地；根本上」
生物学名词，源自同一拉丁词根，义为「原基」，指器官发育的最初细胞团
由形容词加 -ity 构成的抽象名词，义为「原始性」

senses.title: Existing from the very beginning
senses.titleCN: 自最初就存在的；太古的
senses.definition: existing from the earliest period of the world, before anything else was formed
senses.definitionCN: 自世界最早期便存在、在其他事物形成之前就已存在的
senses.example: The land still holds some of the primordial rock of the planet.
senses.exampleCN: 这片土地仍保留着一些地球最古老的岩石。
senses.why: The Latin word is made of first and beginning, so whatever it touches is placed at the very start.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原词就是「第一」加「开端」，所以它修饰的任何事物都被放在了最开头；核心意象里的原始热汤正是这种「一切尚未成形之前」的起点。

senses.title: Basic and forming the foundation
senses.definition: fundamental and lying at the base of something, on which everything else depends
senses.definitionCN: 根本性的、处于事物底层，其他一切都依赖其上的
senses.example: Trust is a primordial element of any team, older than any written rule.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是任何团队的根本要素，比任何成文规则都更早。
senses.why: What comes first also comes before everything else in importance, so the beginning sense turns into a sense of foundation.
senses.whyCN: 最先出现的东西在重要性上也排在一切之前，于是「开端」义自然转为「根基」义；从这个词根长出的 primordiality 等抽象名词也走同一条路。

senses.title: Native rather than learned
senses.definition: present from birth or from the start of a person, not acquired by learning
senses.definitionCN: 自出生或自一开始就具备的，而非后天学来的
senses.example: Curiosity seems primordial in children, long before anyone teaches it.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心在孩子身上似乎是与生俱来的，远在有人教导之前就已存在。
senses.why: If something has been there from the first moment of a life, it counts as innate, and the word lends itself to instincts and drives.
senses.whyCN: 如果某样东西从生命的第一刻起就存在，它就算作天生的；这个词便自然被用来形容本能与冲动。

senses.title: In the earliest stage of biological development
senses.definition: describing cells or tissues at the very first stage of an organ before it takes shape
senses.definitionCN: 形容器官成形之前那一最初阶段的细胞或组织的
senses.example: The embryo contains primordial cells that will later become the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎里含有日后会发育成心脏的原始细胞。
senses.why: Biology keeps the first sense literally, naming the earliest unspecialised cells by the same word, a use borrowed from Latin primordium.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把「第一时期」的字面义保留下来，用同一个词命名最早、尚未分化的细胞，这一用法借自拉丁语名词 primordium。

intro.en: Primordial is formed from Latin primus, first, and ordiri, to begin, itself from ordiri in the sense of starting a web, and was borrowed into English through late Latin primordialis.
intro.cn: primordial 由拉丁语 primus（第一）与 ordiri（开始；起织）构成，经晚期拉丁语形容词 primordialis 传入英语。

items.en: Ordiris means to begin, and in its physical sense to start weaving a web.
items.cn: ordiri 意为开始，其本义是动手织一张网、起一个头。

items.en: The noun primordium means the very beginning, literally the first thread of the web.
items.cn: 名词 primordium 意为开端，字面意思是网线的最初一缕。

items.en: Late Latin builds the adjective primordialis from primordium.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语由 primordium 构成形容词 primordialis。

items.en: English first takes the noun in the form primordie, then the adjective, both meaning a first beginning.
items.cn: 英语先借入名词形式 primordie，再借入形容词，二者都表示「最初的开端」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology revives the Latin noun primordium for the earliest cell groups, and the adjective follows it.
items.cn: 十九世纪的生物学让拉丁名词 primordium 重回使用，指最早的细胞群，形容词随之沿用。

items.en: Modern use adds the created-world broth of primordial soup and the scientific sense of primordial radiation.
items.cn: 现代用法又增添了「原始汤」这一创世图景，以及原始辐射这一科学义项。

note.en: Primordial is a first-beginning word that shares its prim- core with prime and primitive, and sits close to words for the very earliest age.
note.cn: primordial 表示「最初的开端」，与 prime、primitive 共享 prim- 词根，意义上也靠近表达「最早时期」的若干词。

entries.definition: the earliest group of cells for an organ
entries.definitionCN: 器官发育的最初细胞群；原基

entries.definition: the earliest ancestor of a line
entries.definitionCN: 始祖；血统中最初始的祖先

entries.definition: first in order or importance
belonging to the earliest ages of the earth
entries.definitionCN: 太古的；（地球）最古老时期的

entries.definition: inherited from earlier generations
forming the base of something

normalIntro.en: Primordial is first plus beginning: prim gives the first, and the old verb behind it means to start a thread, so the whole word is the first thread of everything.
normalIntro.cn: primordial 就是「第一」加「开端」：prim 表示第一，其后的古动词表示起一缕线，所以整个词就是万物最初的那根线头。

normal.en: Prim means first, as in prime, primary, and primitive, so primordial starts at the first moment.
normal.cn: prim 表示第一，如 prime、primary、primitive，因此 primordial 从最初的一刻开始。

normal.en: The ord part is the Latin verb for beginning, and it also gave order, the arrangement of things.
normal.cn: ord 部分来自表示「开始」的拉丁动词，它同样给了 order（秩序、排列）。

normal.en: Primordial soup is the favourite name for the sea of chemicals where life is thought to have started.
normal.cn: primordial soup 是人们最常用的说法，指生命被认为开始于其中的那片化学之海。

normal.en: In biology a primordium is the first small group of cells, and the adjective describes these very early cells.
normal.cn: 生物学里的 primordium 指最初的少量细胞，形容词正是用来描写这些极早期的细胞。

normal.en: Compare primeval, which stresses an ancient time, with primordial, which stresses the very first start.
normal.cn: 对比 primeval：primeval 强调时代古老，primordial 强调最初的开端。

abstract.en: Picture the first full stop on an empty page, before a single word.
abstract.cn: 想象空白页面上落下的第一个句点，那时还一个字都没有。

abstract.en: Think of the deepest root of a great tree that holds every branch above.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵大树的根基，深深托住上面所有的枝杈。

abstract.en: Watch an infant reach for a bright object long before any lesson.
abstract.cn: 看着婴儿在任何人教之前就伸手去够亮闪闪的东西。

examples.en: Life is thought to have begun in the primordial ocean.
examples.cn: 生命被认为起源于原始海洋。

examples.en: The study examines primordial needs such as food, shelter, and safety.
examples.cn: 这项研究考察食物、住所与安全这类根本需求。

examples.en: The primordial cells divide before the leaf begins to form.
examples.cn: 在叶片开始形成之前，原基细胞先进行分裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普赖莫迪」——「莫」要忘了它，一切的「最开头」总在记忆之前就已存在；把「普」和「最开头」连在一起，就记住了 primordial。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 primus（第一）＋ ordiri（开始；起织）→ 拉丁语名词 primordium（开端）→ 晚期拉丁语 primordialis → 英语 primordial，核心义「最初的开端」。

sensesIntro.en: Primordial starts as the label of the very first beginning, turns into the basis of other things, then into what is inborn, and in biology names the earliest unspecialised cells.
sensesIntro.cn: primordial 起初标记「最初的开端」，进而指其他事物的根基，再指与生俱来的特质，在生物学里则用来命名最早、尚未分化的细胞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first cell bubbling up in a warm swirl before anything has a shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：在万物成形之前的温热漩涡里，冒出第一个细胞。

branches.en: What stands at the very start of time is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 处于时间最开端的事物是这个词的本义。

branches.en: Whatever comes first also underlies the rest, so an onset becomes a base.
branches.cn: 最先出现的东西同样托住其余部分，于是「开端」变成了「基础」。

branches.en: A trait present from the first moment is treated as native.
branches.cn: 从第一刻起就存在的特质，就被看作天生的。

branches.en: Biology keeps the first sense for the first cell groups of an organ.
branches.cn: 生物学把「第一」的字面义保留在器官最初的细胞群上。

branches.en: Both a foundation and a primordium are the quiet base from which later structures grow.
branches.cn: 根基与原基都是后来结构生长的安静底座。

intro.en: Primordial pairs the Latin root prim, first, with a family built on the verb for beginning, and also gives English the technical noun primordium.
intro.cn: primordial 把拉丁词根 prim（第一）与一个以「开始」动词为核心的同族结合在一起，还让英语多出技术名词 primordium。

latinIntro.en: Primus means first, and ordiri means to begin, so primordium is the very beginning, the first thread of a web.
latinIntro.cn: primus 意为第一，ordiri 意为开始，所以 primordium 就是最初的开端，即网的第一缕线。

items.example: The root places the whole word at the start.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把整个词放在了开端的位置。

items.example: Ordiri is the beginning half of the word.
items.exampleCN: ordiri 是这个词表示「开端」的那一半。

items.example: Primordium is the noun that the adjective comes from.
items.exampleCN: primordium 是这个形容词所由来的名词。

items.example: Primordialis is the late Latin model of the English word.
items.exampleCN: primordialis 是英语词的晚期拉丁语原型。

items.example: The ending -al turns the noun into a descriptive adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把名词变成描写性的形容词。

items.structure: English noun from the same verb
items.example: Order shares the starting verb but turned towards arrangement.
items.exampleCN: order 与它同出一个「开始」的动词，但语义转向了排列。

items.meaningCN: 按最初次序排列的（罕用）
items.example: Primordinate is rare today and survives in older scientific writing.
items.exampleCN: primordinate 今天很少用，仅见于较早的科学写作。

items.meaning: the first cell group of an organ
items.meaningCN: 原基；器官的初始细胞群
items.example: Biologists revived the Latin noun as an English technical term.
items.exampleCN: 生物学家把这个拉丁名词重新用作英语术语。

items.example: The ending -ial also appears in material and memorial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 也出现在 material、memorial 等词中。

definition_zh: 私有化；使私营化；将国有或公有资产转为私人所有
definition_en: to transfer a business, service, or industry from state or public ownership to private ownership and control
core_image: 一面写有「国有」的牌子被摘下，换成写有「私营」的小牌，交到私人手里
scene: 市政厅门口挤满了记者，政府刚刚决定把电力公司卖给私人投资者。The council has just decided to privatise the power company and sell it to investors.
sceneCN: 这里 privatise 是「使转为私人所有」（第 1 个义项：把国有产业卖给私人）；句意：市政会刚决定把电力公司私有化，卖给投资者。

pos.zh: 使私有化；把国有（公有）产业转为私营

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「私有化」，指把公有产业转为私营的过程
动词加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「主张或主持私有化的人」
基础形容词，义为「私人的；私有的」，与表示「剥夺」的拉丁词根同源

senses.title: To sell state-owned firms to private owners
senses.definition: to transfer a state-owned company or enterprise into private ownership, usually by selling its shares
senses.definitionCN: 把国有企业转为私人所有，通常通过出售其股份实现
senses.example: The government privatised the national airline in the early nineteen nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在上世纪九十年代初把国家航空公司私有化了。
senses.why: The word is built from private plus the verb-making ending -ise, so the act is literally to make something private, as when a state sign is taken down and replaced.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 private 加上构成动词的后缀 -ise 组成，动作字面就是「使某物成为私人的」；核心意象中摘下「国有」牌子的瞬间，正对应这一动作。

senses.title: To hand a public service to a company
senses.titleCN: 把公共服务交给私营公司经营
senses.definition: to give the running of a public service such as water, rail, or health care to a private business
senses.definitionCN: 把供水、铁路或医疗等公共服务的运营权交给私营企业
senses.example: Many cities privatised their bus networks to cut costs.
senses.exampleCN: 许多城市把公交网络私有化，以削减成本。
senses.why: Once ownership of a company moves to private hands, the service it provides moves with it, so the verb is used for services as well as firms.
senses.whyCN: 一旦企业的所有权转到私人手中，它提供的服务也随之转移，所以这个动词同样用于服务而不仅是公司；核心意象里换牌的动作会沿着产业链一路往下传。

senses.title: To make something private in general
senses.titleCN: 使成为私人性质；使私有
senses.definition: to give a formerly public or shared thing a private character or owner outside the economic debate
senses.definitionCN: 把原本公共或共享之物变成具有私人性质或其私人所有的东西，不限于经济语境
senses.example: Some residents privatised the shared courtyard by building walls and gates.
senses.exampleCN: 一些住户砌墙装门，把共享的院子变成了自家私地。
senses.why: The private part of the word is general, so the verb can describe any shift from shared to private, even without a company or a sale.
senses.whyCN: 词中的 private 本身含义很广，所以这个动词也能描写任何从共享到私有的转变，哪怕没有公司、也没有买卖；这正是核心意象「摘牌换牌」可以放大的地方。

senses.title: To gain privately from a public asset
senses.titleCN: 使公共资源被私人占用取利
senses.definition: to let private interests take control of a public resource and draw profit from it, a use often critical
senses.definitionCN: 让私人利益掌控公共资源并从中获利，这种用法常带批评意味
senses.example: Critics say the government has privatised the profits while keeping the risks public.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说，政府把利润私有化了，却把风险留给了公众。
senses.why: A neutral word for ownership turns into a warning when what is shared is seen as being taken, so privatise can carry disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 一个中性的所有权词，在共有之物被视为被拿走时就会变成警告，因此 privatise 也能带出不满；这与核心意象中牌子被谁拿走、谁能进门的关注点相呼应。

intro.en: Privatise is an English formation from the Latin adjective privatus, private, with the rare verb-making ending -ise imitating older -ate words; the form dates from the late eighteenth century and the economic sense from the twentieth.
intro.cn: privatise 是英语自造的动词，由拉丁语形容词 privatus（私人的）加动词词尾 -ise 构成，模仿更早的 -ate 类词；词形见于十八世纪末，经济义则出现于二十世纪。

items.en: Privare means to set apart or strip away, and privatus means belonging to an individual rather than to the state.
items.cn: privare 意为分开或剥夺，privatus 意为属于个人而不是国家的。

items.en: Privatus is the past participle of privare, so the private is what has been set apart from the public.
items.cn: privatus 是 privare 的过去分词，所以「私人的」就是被从公共中分出来的部分。

items.en: Privatus passes through late Latin as privatus into Old French as prive, then into English as private.
items.cn: privatus 经晚期拉丁语传入古法语作 prive，再进入英语成为 private。

items.en: Eighteenth-century English adds -ise to private for the verb privatise, first in a general sense.
items.cn: 十八世纪的英语在 private 后加 -ise 造出动词 privatise，最初是一般义。

items.en: After the Second World War, privatise and privatisation take on the modern meaning of selling state assets, and the form becomes common in British news.
items.cn: 二战后，privatise 与 privatisation 获得了出售国有资产的现代含义，这一词形在英国新闻中变得常见。

note.en: Privatise is the verb form of private, and in British spelling it pairs with a noun and an adjective built from the same base.
note.cn: privatise 是 private 构成的动词，在英式拼写下它与同一词根派生出的名词、形容词配套使用。

entries.definition: the act of selling a public firm to private owners
entries.definitionCN: 私有化；把公有企业出售给私人

entries.definition: the American spelling of the same verb
entries.definitionCN: 同一个动词的美式拼写

entries.definition: belonging to one person rather than the state
to move a private company into state ownership
entries.definitionCN: 使国有化；把私营企业收归国家

entries.definition: to remove official rules from an industry
entries.definitionCN: 放松管制；取消对某行业的官方规定

entries.definition: to give work to an outside company
entries.definitionCN: 外包；把工作交给外部公司

normalIntro.en: Privatise is simply private made into a verb: the -ise ending means to make, so the word means to make something private.
normalIntro.cn: privatise 就是把 private 变成动词：后缀 -ise 表示「使成为」，所以这个词的意思就是「使……成为私有的」。

normal.en: Private is the base, and the ending -ise is one of the standard endings for making verbs in British English.
normal.cn: private 是基础词，而词尾 -ise 是英式英语构成动词的常用词尾之一。

normal.en: Add -ation and you get privatisation, the name for the policy of selling public firms.
normal.cn: 加上 -ation 就得到 privatisation，它指出售公有企业的政策。

normal.en: American English spells it with z, so you will see privatize in United States newspapers.
normal.cn: 美式英语用字母 z 拼写，所以美国报纸上会写成 privatize。

normal.en: The opposite verb is nationalise, which moves a firm back into the hands of the state.
normal.cn: 反义动词是 nationalise，意思是把企业重新收回国家手中。

normal.en: Private itself comes from Latin privare, to set apart, so a private firm is one cut away from the public body.
normal.cn: private 本身来自拉丁语 privare（分开），因此私营公司就是从公共机构中分离出来的一家。

abstract.en: Picture a sign on a factory gate being unscrewed and replaced with another.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂门口的牌子被拧下来，换上一块新的。

abstract.en: Imagine a key changing hands from a clerk at a counter to an investor in a suit.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙从柜台后的职员手里，交到一位西装革履的投资者手中。

abstract.en: See a shared park slowly cut into private gardens with garden walls.
abstract.cn: 看着一座共享的公园被一堵堵围墙慢慢切分成一块块私家花园。

examples.en: The government plans to privatise the postal service next year.
examples.cn: 政府计划明年把邮政服务私有化。

examples.en: Several hospitals were privatised after the new law was passed.
examples.cn: 新法律通过后，有几家医院被私有化了。

examples.en: Opponents argue that the scheme would privatise clean water.
examples.cn: 反对者认为，这项计划会把清洁的水源私有化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普赖维太兹」——「赖」在原处不动的公共产业，被「维」系到私人手里、「太」贵地卖掉；把「私人」两个字牢牢安在词尾的 -ise 上，就记住了 privatise。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 privare（分开、剥夺）→ 过去分词 privatus（私人的）→ 古法语 prive → 英语 private（私人的）；再以英语动词词尾 -ise 构成 privatise，核心义「使成为私人的」。

sensesIntro.en: Privatise starts with selling a state-owned company, then covers handing over public services, expands to any move from shared to private, and can carry a critical tone when the public loses out.
sensesIntro.cn: privatise 从卖掉国有企业说起，接着指把公共服务交给私营公司，再扩展到任何「从共享到私有」的转变，且当公众受损时常带批评口气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a state sign being taken down and an individual key being handed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：国有牌子被摘下，一把私人钥匙被交出去。

branches.en: Selling a state firm is the economic sense that made the word famous.
branches.cn: 出售国有企业是让这个词广为人知的经济义项。

branches.en: A service owned by a private firm is run by that firm, so the verb reaches services.
branches.cn: 由私营企业拥有的服务就由该企业运营，所以这个动词也用到了服务上。

branches.en: Outside economics the word simply marks a move from shared to private.
branches.cn: 在经济之外，这个词只标记从共享到私有的转变。

branches.en: When the public feels robbed, the neutral ownership word becomes criticism.
branches.cn: 当公众觉得自己被夺走利益时，这个中性的所有权词就变成了批评。

branches.en: The same sale can be described as a good deal or as private gain at public cost.
branches.cn: 同一次出售，既可以被称为划算的交易，也可以被称为以公众为代价的私人获益。

intro.en: Privatise combines the Latin-derived private with the verb-making ending -ise, and the wider family brings -ation and -er into English.
intro.cn: privatise 由源自拉丁语的 private 加动词词尾 -ise 构成，整个词族又通过 -ation 与 -er 等词尾扩展出英语新词。

latinIntro.en: Latin privare means to set apart or strip away, and its participle privatus means belonging to an individual.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 privare 意为分开或剥夺，其分词 privatus 意为属于个人的。

items.example: The root carries the idea of being cut away from the whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带有从整体中被切下来的意思。

items.example: Privare gives private its core of being set apart.
items.exampleCN: privare 给了 private「被分出来」这一核心义。

items.example: Privatus is the direct ancestor of private.
items.exampleCN: privatus 是 private 的直接祖先。

items.meaning: belonging to a person, not the state
items.example: Private is the base of the whole modern family.
items.exampleCN: private 是整个现代词族的基础。

items.example: The ending -ise turns adjectives into verbs such as privatise.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ise 把形容词变成像 privatise 这样的动词。

items.example: The same ending appears as -ize in privatize.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词尾在 privatize 中写作 -ize。

items.example: The ending -ation forms privatisation from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 由动词构成 privatisation。

items.example: The ending -er forms privatiser, one who carries out the sale.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 privatiser，指主持这场出售的人。

items.meaning: to bring a private firm under the state
items.example: Nationalise uses the same -ise ending with the opposite effect.
items.exampleCN: nationalise 用同样的 -ise 词尾，效果却正相反。

items.structure: English noun from the same verb
items.meaning: the state of being without something
items.example: Deprivation shares the Latin verb for stripping away.
items.exampleCN: deprivation 与其共享那个表示「剥夺」的拉丁动词。

definition_zh: 缓刑；试用期；见习期
definition_en: a period during which a person or thing is tested before being fully accepted or punished
core_image: 一根木棒把新员工轻轻推开：先站在门外试一试，通过才放进来
scene: 新律师进所的头三个月要边干边学，合伙人会一直观察。The young lawyer spent three months on probation before becoming a full partner.
sceneCN: 这里 probation 是「试用期、见习期」（第 2 个义项：考察工作能力的期限）；句意：那位年轻律师在成为正式合伙人之前，先经过了三个月的试用期。

derivatives.zh: 由 probation 加 -ary 构成，义为「试用的；缓刑考验的」
由 probation 加 -er 构成，义为「试用人员；缓刑犯」
与 probation 同出拉丁语 probare，义为「证明；证实」
同源词，原指「证明」，现指遗嘱的认证

senses.title: A suspended sentence
senses.definition: a legal arrangement in which a guilty person is released under supervision instead of being sent to prison
senses.definitionCN: 法律上让有罪的人接受监督而不入狱服刑的安排
senses.example: The judge put him on probation for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 法官判他缓刑一年。
senses.why: The Latin root probare means to test, and a suspended sentence is the law testing whether the offender can behave.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 probare 意为「检验」，缓刑就是法律先考察罪犯能否守规矩，这正是一段测试期。

senses.title: A trial period at work
senses.definition: a period at the start of a job or training when a person is watched and judged
senses.definitionCN: 在工作或培训之初，受观察与评定的时期
senses.example: New staff are on probation for the first half year.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工在头半年处于试用期。
senses.why: The same testing idea extends from courts to employers, who try a newcomer before offering a permanent post.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「检验」思路从法庭延伸到雇主，雇主先把新人放进试用期，再决定是否长期聘用。

senses.title: A period of watchfulness
senses.definition: any stated span of time in which something is watched for signs of success or failure
senses.definitionCN: 任何被明确指定的、用来观察成败迹象的时间段
senses.example: The new policy is still within its probation period.
senses.exampleCN: 新政策仍在考察期内。
senses.why: Once the word names a span of time rather than a legal status, it can cover any policy, product, or system put to the test.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词从法律身份变成一段时间，它就能指任何被拿来检验的政策、产品或制度。

senses.title: A state of being tested
senses.definition: the condition of being under test before full approval is given
senses.definitionCN: 在获得完全认可之前处于受检验的状态
senses.example: The experimental system remained in probation for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验系统在两年的时间里一直处于受检验的状态。
senses.why: The word can also describe not the period but the ongoing condition of never yet being fully trusted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以不指那段时间本身，而指「始终还没被完全信任」的持续状态。

intro.en: Probation comes from Latin probatio, a testing, from probare, to test or prove.
intro.cn: probation 来自拉丁语 probatio（检验），源自动词 probare（检验、证明）。

items.en: Probare means to test, examine, or prove; its noun probatio is a testing.
items.cn: probare 意为检验、考察、证明，其名词 probatio 意为检验。

items.en: Christian writers use the word for a time of trial and moral testing.
items.cn: 基督教作者用这个词表示受考验、受道德检验的时期。

items.en: Probacion carries the sense of testing and proof into French.
items.cn: probacion 把检验与证明的含义带入法语。

items.en: Probation appears in English for a time of trial or proof.
items.cn: probation 在中古英语中出现，指受考验、经受验证的时期。

items.en: Laws adopting probation for offenders make the legal sense standard.
items.cn: 十九世纪关于缓刑的法律使这一法律义项成为常用义。

items.en: Business adds the trial period for new employees.
items.cn: 现代英语中商界又加入了新员工的试用期用法。

note.en: Probation belongs to the probare family of testing words, and it sits near legal and workplace terms about supervision.
note.cn: probation 属于 probare（检验）这一词族，同时与法学和职场中关于监管的词相邻。

entries.definition: relating to a trial period
a person on probation
to show that something is true
the official proving of a will
release from prison with a promise of good behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 假释（与 probation 不同，probation 可代替入狱）

entries.definition: a temporary stopping of a punishment or duty
a test period of trying something out

normalIntro.en: Probation is Latin probare at work: someone must prove themselves for a while before full trust.
normalIntro.cn: probation 就是拉丁语 probare（检验）在工作：某人得先证明自己一段时间，才能获得完全信任。

normal.en: On probation means a person or a job is still being tested.
normal.cn: on probation 表示某人或某项工作仍处于检验之中。

normal.en: The probation period is the first stage of any new job.
normal.cn: probation period 是任何新工作的第一阶段。

normal.en: Prove and probation share the same testing root.
normal.cn: prove 与 probation 共享「检验」这一词根。

normal.en: A judge places an offender on probation instead of in prison.
normal.cn: 法官把罪犯判入缓刑，而不是投入监狱。

normal.en: Compare parole: parole follows a prison term, while probation may replace it.
normal.cn: 对比 parole：假释在刑期之后，而 probation 可以代替入狱。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden bar gently holding a newcomer at the door of a room.
abstract.cn: 想象一根木棒轻轻把一个新人拦在门口。

abstract.en: See a name badge printed with the word trainee.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚胸牌，上面印着实习生字样。

abstract.en: Think of a timer counting down while a supervisor takes notes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个倒计时器在走，主管在一旁记笔记。

examples.en: She served her probation and avoided a prison sentence.
examples.cn: 她服完缓刑，避免了入狱服刑。

examples.en: Employees are reviewed at the end of probation.
examples.cn: 员工在试用期结束时接受考评。

examples.en: The new method is still on probation in three schools.
examples.cn: 新方法还在三所学校试行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若背身」——新人先被推到一边、背对着门，考察过关才转身进门；这只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 probare（检验、证明）→ probatio（检验）→ 古法语 probacion → 英语 probation，核心义「先检验、后正式接纳」。

sensesIntro.en: Probation begins as a legal test of an offender, then the test extends to a new employee, to any stated watching period, and finally to the lasting condition of being tested.
sensesIntro.cn: probation 从对罪犯的法律考验起步，接着把考验延伸到新员工，再泛化为任何明文规定的观察期，最后指始终处于被检验的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden bar holding a newcomer back until the test is passed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根木棒把新人挡在门外，直到检验通过。

branches.en: The court sense is the oldest one: the law tests rather than imprisons.
branches.cn: 法庭义是最早的义项：法律选择考验而不是监禁。

branches.en: The work sense moves the same test from courts to employers.
branches.cn: 职场义把同样的考验从法庭搬到雇主那里。

branches.en: Any policy or product can have its own watchful period.
branches.cn: 任何政策或产品都可以有自己的考察期。

branches.en: Both are fixed spans of time set aside for judging results.
branches.cn: 两者都是为评判结果而划出的固定时间段。

branches.en: A suspended sentence leaves a person in an ongoing state of being watched.
branches.cn: 缓刑把人留在一种持续受监视的状态中。

intro.en: Probation is built from the Latin testing verb probare, with English -ary and -er forms growing from the noun.
intro.cn: probation 由拉丁语表示检验的动词 probare 构成，英语里又从名词长出 -ary 与 -er 两种形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare means to test or prove, and probatio is the act of testing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验、证明，probatio 意为检验这一行为。

items.example: Probare supplies the testing idea.
items.exampleCN: probare 提供检验之意。

items.example: Probatio is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: probatio 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion turns probare into probation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 把 probare 变成 probation。

items.meaning: to show that something is true
items.example: Prove keeps the testing root in everyday English.
items.exampleCN: prove 在日常英语中保留「检验」词根。

items.example: The suffix -ary forms probationary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 构成 probationary。

items.example: Probationary describes the trial stage of employment.
items.exampleCN: probationary 描述用工的试用阶段。

items.meaning: a person who or thing that
items.example: The suffix -er forms probationer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 probationer。

items.example: Probationer names the person under test.
items.exampleCN: probationer 指处于受检验中的人。

items.meaning: the official proving of a will
items.example: Probate is the same root used in law.
items.exampleCN: probate 是同一词根的法律用法。

items.example: Approbation shows what passing the test brings.
items.exampleCN: approbation 展示了通过检验后得到的认可。

definition_zh: 探查；调查；探针；探测器
definition_en: to examine something closely, or a thin tool used for examining
core_image: 一根细长的金属针慢慢伸进缝隙里，试探里面到底有什么
scene: 医生手持一根细长的仪器，轻轻探入病人的耳道检查。The doctor used a thin probe to look inside the patients ear.
sceneCN: 这里 probe 是「探针、探测仪器」（第 1 个义项：用来探查的细长器具）；句意：医生用一根细探针查看病人的耳朵内部。

derivatives.zh: 由 probe 加 -ing 构成，义为「追根究底的；探查性的」
由 probe 加 -ing 构成名词，义为「探查；探测」
与 probe 同出拉丁语 probare，义为「缓刑；试用期」

senses.title: A thin examining tool
senses.definition: a slender instrument used to examine a place that cannot be seen directly
senses.definitionCN: 用来检查无法直接看到之处的细长器械
senses.example: The surgeon checked the canal with a fine probe.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生用一根细探针检查了那条通道。
senses.why: The slender tool carries the core image most literally: length plus a pointed tip lets it reach what the eye cannot.
senses.whyCN: 细长的工具最直接地承载核心意象：长度加尖头，使它能够抵达眼睛看不见的地方。

senses.title: To search by feeling
senses.definition: to examine something by pushing or feeling into it
senses.definitionCN: 通过推入或触摸来检查某物
senses.example: He probed the soil with a stick.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一根棍子戳探土壤。
senses.why: The verb takes the tool and moves it, so testing becomes a physical action of feeling around in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 动词拿起工具开始移动，于是检验变成在黑暗中摸索的物理动作。

senses.title: To investigate closely
senses.definition: to ask careful questions in order to find out the truth
senses.definitionCN: 通过仔细提问来查明真相
senses.example: Reporters probed the ministers spending.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们深入调查了那位部长的开支。
senses.why: Words can probe too, so a careful question becomes the needle that goes after hidden facts.
senses.whyCN: 言辞也能发挥探针的作用，因此一句仔细的追问就成了追查隐藏事实的那根针。

senses.title: An unmanned exploring craft
senses.definition: a spacecraft sent to explore a place without people on board
senses.definitionCN: 无人驾驶、被送往某地探测的航天器
senses.example: The probe sent back pictures of the moons surface.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器传回了月球表面的照片。
senses.why: A craft sent to another planet is the needle stretched across space, testing a place nobody can touch.
senses.whyCN: 被派往另一颗行星的飞行器，就是把那根针拉到太空尺度，去检验一个没人能碰到的地方。

senses.title: An official inquiry
senses.definition: a formal investigation into a matter of public concern
senses.definitionCN: 对公众关注事项进行的正式调查
senses.example: The city opened a probe into the missing funds.
senses.exampleCN: 市政当局对失踪资金展开了调查。
senses.why: An official probe keeps the legal search behind the first English use of the word and turns it into a public act.
senses.whyCN: 官方调查保留了这个词在英语中最早的「依法搜查」含义，并把它变成一项公开行为。

intro.en: Probe is probably from Latin probare, to test, itself of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: probe 一般认为来自拉丁语 probare（检验），而 probare 本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Probare means to test or examine; its own source is uncertain.
items.cn: probare 意为检验、考察，其来源本身不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin proba names an official examination or inspection.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 proba 指官方的检查、查验。

items.en: Probe first names a legal search for evidence.
items.cn: 英语中的 probe 最初指为取证而进行的搜查。

items.en: Surgery adopts probe for a slender instrument for examining wounds.
items.cn: 外科借 probe 指检查伤口用的细长器械。

items.en: Space science gives the word its spacecraft sense.
items.cn: 太空科学赋予这个词「航天探测器」的新义。

items.en: Journalists use the verb for any deep investigation.
items.cn: 现代英语中记者用这个动词泛指各种深入调查。

note.en: Probe is the tip of the testing family: it is the tool that tests and the act of testing.
note.cn: probe 处于「检验」语义家族的前端：它既是检验的工具，也是检验的动作。

entries.definition: searching and thorough
a period of testing a person
to show that something is true
the official proving of a will
to look into a matter carefully
entries.definitionCN: 调查（比 probe 更中性、更常用）

entries.definition: to look at something closely
to travel through a place to learn about it

normalIntro.en: Probe is a needle that tests: the verb pushes in to find out, and the noun is the pushing tool.
normalIntro.cn: probe 是一根用来试探的针：动词是往里推以查明，名词就是这根推的针。

normal.en: A space probe explores a place no person can reach.
normal.cn: space probe 探索人无法抵达的地方。

normal.en: To probe into a matter is to dig for the truth.
normal.cn: probe into 某事，就是把真相挖出来。

normal.en: Police probe usually means a formal investigation.
normal.cn: police probe 通常指正式的警方调查。

normal.en: A surgeon probes a wound before stitching it.
normal.cn: 外科医生缝合前先探查伤口。

normal.en: Compare investigate: probe is shorter and often suggests something secret.
normal.cn: 对比 investigate：probe 更简短，常暗示涉及隐秘之事。

abstract.en: Picture a needle sliding into a dark crack and meeting something hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一根针滑进黑暗的裂缝，碰到一个硬东西。

abstract.en: Think of a finger tapping a wall to hear where the hollow spot is.
abstract.cn: 想象用手指敲墙，听哪里是空心的。

abstract.en: See a tiny craft drifting past a planet, sending back pictures.
abstract.cn: 想象一架小小的飞行器掠过行星，传回照片。

examples.en: The probe travelled for years before reaching the planet.
examples.cn: 这架探测器飞行多年才抵达那颗行星。

examples.en: Officials are probing how the fire started.
examples.cn: 官员们正在调查火灾是如何发生的。

examples.en: She probed the dark space under the shelf with her fingers.
examples.cn: 她用手指在架子下方的黑暗处摸索。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑萝卜」——手伸进地里扑着找萝卜，也就是用一根针探进去试；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 probare（检验）→ 中世纪拉丁语 proba（查验）→ 英语 probe，核心义「伸进去试一试」。

sensesIntro.en: Probe starts as a slender testing tool, then shifts to the act of testing by touch, then to careful questioning, and finally to the machines and formal inquiries that carry the search far away.
sensesIntro.cn: probe 从一件细长的检验工具起步，转为用触碰去试探的动作，再转为仔细追问，最后指把这种搜寻推向远方的机器与正式调查。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin needle pushed into a gap to find out what lies inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细针伸进缝隙，查清里面有什么。

branches.en: The tool sense keeps the concrete needle image.
branches.cn: 工具义保留了具体的针这一画面。

branches.en: The feeling sense turns the tool into an action.
branches.cn: 触碰义把工具转化为动作。

branches.en: Questioning sense uses words as the needle.
branches.cn: 调查义把言辞当作那根针。

branches.en: Space probes are the needle stretched to planetary scale.
branches.cn: 太空探测器就是把那根针放大到行星尺度。

branches.en: Both senses look for hidden facts, one by reporters and one by officials.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在找隐藏的事实，一个靠记者，一个靠官方。

intro.en: Probe has no productive English affix of its own; its power comes from the shared Latin testing root.
intro.cn: probe 自身没有能产的英语词缀，它的力量来自与同族词共享的拉丁语检验词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare means to test, and the short form proba names a check or examination.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 probare 意为检验，短形式 proba 指查验、检查。

items.example: Probare gives the family its testing idea.
items.exampleCN: probare 为整个词族提供检验之意。

items.example: Proba is the likely bridge to English probe.
items.exampleCN: proba 很可能是通向英语 probe 的桥梁。

items.example: Probe splits the two jobs of the word.
items.exampleCN: probe 同时承担工具与动作两重身份。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms probing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 probing。

items.example: Probing questions go deep.
items.exampleCN: probing 的问题会问到底。

items.meaning: to show that something is true
items.example: Prove is the plain verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: prove 是该词族中最朴素的动词。

items.example: Probation tests a person over time.
items.exampleCN: probation 在一段时间里考验一个人。

items.meaning: the official proving of a will
items.example: Probate shows the legal side of the root.
items.exampleCN: probate 展示该词根的法律用法。

items.example: Improbable uses the same root with a negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: improbable 用同一词根加否定前缀构成。

definition_zh: 宣布；宣告；声明；表明
definition_en: to say something publicly and firmly, so that everyone knows it
core_image: 一个人站上广场的高台，对着人群大声喊出正式决定
scene: 广场上人们聚拢，市长站上台阶向全城宣读决定。The mayor proclaimed a public holiday to celebrate the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 proclaim 是「宣布、宣告」（第 1 个义项：正式而公开地宣布某事）；句意：市长宣布了一个公共假日来庆祝丰收。

derivatives.zh: 由 proclaim 加 -tion 构成，义为「公告；宣告」
由 proclaim 加 -er 构成，义为「宣告者；宣布者」
与 proclaim 同出拉丁语 clamare，义为「声称；索取」
同源词，保留 clamare「喊叫」的本义，义为「大声喧嚷」

senses.title: To announce officially in public
senses.definition: to make an official or formal announcement so that everyone knows
senses.definitionCN: 正式公开地宣布，让所有人都知道
senses.example: The council proclaimed the opening of the new library.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会宣布新图书馆正式开幕。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to shout in front of people, so an official announcement is the most literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为在人前喊出，所以正式的官方宣布是最字面的义项。

senses.title: To say something forcefully
senses.definition: to state something strongly and openly in front of others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人面前用力而公开地表明某事
senses.example: He proclaimed his innocence to the whole crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 他当着众人宣称自己无辜。
senses.why: The same shout can be personal: the speaker drops the official role and only keeps the force of voice.
senses.whyCN: 同一次呼喊也可以是个人的：说话者去掉官方身份，只保留声音的力度。

senses.title: To show something plainly
senses.definition: to make a fact or feeling obvious without saying it
senses.definitionCN: 不靠言语就让事实或情感清楚地显现
senses.example: The ruined walls proclaim the age of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 残破的墙壁显露出这座房子的年代。
senses.why: When a thing speaks for itself, no voice is needed, yet the sign is still as plain as a shout.
senses.whyCN: 当事物不证自明时，不需要人开口，但这种迹象仍像一声呼喊一样清楚。

senses.title: Declaring someone a role
senses.definition: to name a person as ruler, winner, or holder of a title in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式方式指定某人为统治者、胜者或某个头衔的持有者
senses.example: They proclaimed her queen at the start of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在年初宣布她为女王。
senses.why: Naming a king or a champion is still a public call-out, this time turning the act into an official title.
senses.whyCN: 宣布国王或冠军仍属于公开呼喊，只是这一次把这一行为变成正式头衔。

senses.title: To celebrate or praise grandly
senses.definition: to praise someone or something in public and in glowing terms
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合用华丽的言辞赞扬某人或某物
senses.example: The speech proclaimed the courage of the volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇演讲颂扬了志愿者的勇气。
senses.why: Praise spoken aloud to a crowd carries the same shout, with admiration instead of an order behind it.
senses.whyCN: 对人群高声赞扬仍是同一种呼喊，只是背后是敬佩而非命令。

intro.en: Proclaim comes from Latin proclamare, literally to call out in front of people, built from pro- and clamare.
intro.cn: proclaim 来自拉丁语 proclamare，字面意为在众人面前喊出来，由 pro- 与 clamare 构成。

items.en: Clamare means to cry out or shout; pro- adds the sense of openly, in front of.
items.cn: clamare 意为呼喊、喊叫，pro- 加上「公开地、在人前」之意。

items.en: Proclamare means to call out, to summon, or to declare openly.
items.cn: proclamare 意为呼喊、召集或公开宣布。

items.en: Proclamation becomes a standard word for a public act of authority.
items.cn: 在中世纪，proclamation 成为表示当权者公开宣告的标准用词。

items.en: Proclamer carries the French form of the word.
items.cn: proclamer 是该词的法语形式。

items.en: Proclaim appears in English with the meaning to announce publicly.
items.cn: proclaim 在中古英语中出现，意为公开宣布。

items.en: The figurative use in journalism extends the word to plain signs and praise.
items.cn: 现代英语中新闻写作的比喻用法，把词义扩展到明显的迹象与赞扬。

note.en: Proclaim belongs to the clamare shouting family and sits beside words for public announcement and declaration.
note.cn: proclaim 属于 clamare（呼喊）词族，同时与表示公开宣布、声明的词相邻。

entries.definition: an official public announcement
to say that something is true or yours
to cry out suddenly
to praise someone loudly and publicly
to state something officially and firmly
entries.definitionCN: 宣布；声明（比 proclaim 更中性、更常用）

entries.definition: to make known to people
to say strongly that something is wrong

normalIntro.en: Proclaim is pro- plus clamare: literally to shout a thing out in front of everybody.
normalIntro.cn: proclaim 是 pro- 加 clamare：字面就是在众人面前把它喊出来。

normal.en: To proclaim independence is to tell the whole world it is now free.
normal.cn: proclaim independence 就是向全世界宣布如今已经自由。

normal.en: A proclamation is the written record of what was proclaimed.
normal.cn: proclamation 是被宣告之事的书面记录。

normal.en: Claim shows the same root without the shouting prefix.
normal.cn: claim 展示出同一词根，只是少了表示呼喊的前缀。

normal.en: Exclaim keeps the sudden cry, as in a shout of surprise.
normal.cn: exclaim 保留了突然叫喊之意，如惊叫。

normal.en: Compare declare: declare is quieter and more neutral than proclaim.
normal.cn: 对比 declare：declare 更平和中性，proclaim 更强调声势。

abstract.en: Picture a figure on a high platform with one hand raised and a scroll unrolled.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在高台上，一只手举起，一卷公文展开。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd on the square repeating the words of the speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象广场上的人群跟着讲者重复那些话。

abstract.en: See a crumbling wall that tells the houses age without words.
abstract.cn: 想象一面残墙，不用言语就说出房子的年纪。

examples.en: The government proclaimed a state of emergency after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，政府宣布进入紧急状态。

examples.en: Her calm face proclaimed that all was well.
examples.cn: 她平静的面容表明一切都好。

examples.en: The crowd proclaimed him champion of the town.
examples.cn: 人群宣布他为全镇的冠军。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑到客来」——有什么消息要扑到客人面前大声喊出来；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ clamare（呼喊）→ proclamare（公开喊出）→ 古法语 proclamer → 英语 proclaim，核心义「公开喊出、宣告」。

sensesIntro.en: Proclaim keeps the image of a public shout: it starts as official announcement, then forceful personal statement, then a sign that speaks for itself, then the naming of a title, and finally grand public praise.
sensesIntro.cn: proclaim 保留了「当众喊出」的意象：先指官方宣布，再指用力声明，再指不言自明的迹象，接着指授予某个称号，最后指盛赞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person on a high platform shouting an official decision to the crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在高台上，向人群大声宣读正式决定。

branches.en: The official sense is the closest to the Latin shout.
branches.cn: 官方义最接近拉丁语「呼喊」的本义。

branches.en: The personal sense drops the office and keeps the loudness.
branches.cn: 个人声明义去掉职权，只留下声量。

branches.en: A thing can speak too, so a ruined wall announces its age.
branches.cn: 事物也能「说话」，所以残墙能自报年纪。

branches.en: Both are formal acts that change or confirm someone status.
branches.cn: 两者都是改变或确认某人身份的正式行为。

branches.en: Loud public speech is the common thread between declaring and praising.
branches.cn: 公开大声地说话，是声明与颂扬之间共同的线索。

intro.en: Proclaim pairs the Latin prefix pro- with the shouting verb clamare, with English -ation and -er forms built on it.
intro.cn: proclaim 把拉丁语前缀 pro- 与表示呼喊的动词 clamare 配在一起，英语又在其上构成 -ation 与 -er 形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin clamare means to cry out or shout, and proclamare means to call out publicly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clamare 意为呼喊、喊叫，proclamare 意为公开喊出。

items.example: The prefix pro- adds the idea of speaking in front of people.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 加上「在人前说话」之意。

items.example: Clamare supplies the shout inside the word.
items.exampleCN: clamare 为这个词提供呼喊的内核。

items.example: Proclamare is the direct source of proclaim.
items.exampleCN: proclamare 是 proclaim 的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或其结果的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms proclamation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 proclamation。

items.example: Proclamation names the written act of declaring.
items.exampleCN: proclamation 指宣告行为及其文本。

items.example: The suffix -er forms proclaimer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 proclaimer。

items.example: Proclaimer names the one who shouts the news.
items.exampleCN: proclaimer 指宣告消息的那个人。

items.meaning: to state or demand as a right
items.example: Claim keeps the same root without the prefix.
items.exampleCN: claim 保留同一词根，但没有前缀。

items.example: Exclaim shows the same shouting root in everyday use.
items.exampleCN: exclaim 在日常用法中展示同样的「呼喊」词根。

items.example: Acclaim keeps the loudness for praise.
items.exampleCN: acclaim 把声量用在了赞扬上。

items.example: Clamour preserves the plain meaning of shouting.
items.exampleCN: clamour 保留了呼喊的朴素含义。

definition_zh: 公告；宣言；宣布；声明；公告文书
definition_en: an official public statement made to a large audience, or the act of announcing such a statement
core_image: 官员站上高台，向广场人群高声读出一张盖印的文告
scene: 新法令颁布那天，市民在市政厅台阶前围成一圈。A royal proclamation ordered all shops to close before sunset.
sceneCN: 这里 proclamation 是「公告；文告」（第 1 个义项：官方公开宣布并发布的正式声明）；句意：一道王室公告命令所有店铺在日落前关门。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词「公开宣布」，名词 proclamation 由它加 -ation 转来
公告性质的；宣告式的，后接 -ory 形容词词尾
公告者；宣告者，动词加 -er 表示施事者

senses.title: An official public announcement
senses.definition: an official public statement issued by a ruler or government and addressed to every member of the public
senses.definitionCN: 由统治者或政府发布、面向全体公众的正式公开声明
senses.example: The governor signed a proclamation declaring the harvest day a public holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 州长签署了一份公告，宣布丰收日为公共假日。
senses.why: The Latin verb proclamare meant to cry out in public, so the noun names the words shouted out to the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「当众高声喊出」，所以这个名词指的就是喊给众人听的那番话。

senses.title: The act of announcing formally
senses.definition: the act of announcing something important openly and with official authority
senses.definitionCN: 以官方权威公开地宣告重要事项的行为
senses.example: The proclamation of peace was greeted with church bells.
senses.exampleCN: 和平的宣告响起时，教堂钟声齐鸣。
senses.why: The -ation ending turns the shouting into a process, so the word can name the ceremony of making things public rather than the paper itself.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ation 把「喊出」变成一种过程，于是这个词也能指宣布这件事的行为或仪式，而不只是那张纸。

senses.title: A formal written document
senses.definition: the printed or written text of such an announcement, often sealed and posted where everyone can read it
senses.definitionCN: 这类公告的印刷或书面文本，通常加盖印章并张贴在人人都能看到的地方
senses.example: A copy of the proclamation was nailed to the door of the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 公告的副本被钉在市政厅门上。
senses.why: Once the words are written down and displayed, the act of shouting settles into a physical document.
senses.whyCN: 喊出的话一旦被写下来并张贴出去，那个动作就沉淀成了一件看得见摸得着的文书。

senses.title: A proclamation of a fact
senses.definition: a strong, open declaration of a belief, quality, or intention, often by someone who wants others to notice it
senses.definitionCN: 对某种信念、品质或意图的强烈公开表明，往往意在让别人注意到
senses.example: Her handmade dress was a proclamation of her own style.
senses.exampleCN: 她亲手做的裙子是她个人风格的公开宣言。
senses.why: Because a public shout makes private things visible, the word moves from rulers to anyone who declares something openly to the world.
senses.whyCN: 因为当众喊出来就是把私密的东西摆到明处，这个词便从统治者扩展到任何向世界公开表明态度的人。

senses.title: In Australian football
senses.definition: the loud call made by a player waving a white flag to begin the second half of a match
senses.definitionCN: 澳式橄榄球中球员挥白旗并大声呼喊以开始下半场比赛
senses.example: The crowd roared as the player ran out for the proclamation.
senses.exampleCN: 球员跑出去做赛前宣告时，观众一片欢呼。
senses.why: Even in a sports rulebook the word keeps its cry-out-in-public shape: the umpire makes the restart of play known to everyone at once.
senses.whyCN: 即便写进体育规则，这个词仍保留「当众喊出」的原形：裁判把比赛重新开始的消息一次性告知全场。

intro.en: Proclamation comes through Old French from Latin proclamare, built on pro- (forth, in public) and clamare (to cry out).
intro.cn: proclamation 经古法语来自拉丁语 proclamare，由 pro-（向前、当众）与 clamare（呼喊）构成。

items.en: Clamare means to cry out, and pro means forth or in public.
items.cn: clamare 意为高声呼喊，pro 意为向前、当众。

items.en: Proclamare means to cry out publicly, as a herald does.
items.cn: proclamare 意为当众喊出，就像传令官那样。

items.en: Proclamatio names the act of making a public cry or declaration.
items.cn: proclamatio 指当众呼喊或宣告的行为。

items.en: Proclamacion carries the noun into French law and ceremony.
items.cn: proclamacion 把这个名词带入法语的法律与礼仪领域。

items.en: The word enters English as a public declaration issued by an authority.
items.cn: 该词进入英语，指由当权者发布的公开声明。

items.en: Modern English also uses it for personal declarations and sports calls.
items.cn: 现代英语还用它指个人的公开表明以及体育比赛的宣告。

note.en: Proclamation belongs with proclaim, claim, and clamour, and sits close to other words for public announcements.
note.cn: proclamation 与 proclaim、claim、clamour 同根（都含「呼喊」义），同时也与表示公开声明的其他词相邻。

entries.definition: to announce something publicly and officially
having the nature of a public announcement
to cry out suddenly because of strong feeling
loud and confused noise, especially of many voices
a formal statement made to give people information
a formal statement said in an official way
an official order given by a ruler or government

normalIntro.en: Proclamation is the noun of proclaim: pro- means forth, and clamare means to cry out, so it is a cry sent out to the public.
normalIntro.cn: proclamation 是 proclaim 的名词：pro- 表示「向前」，clamare 表示「呼喊」，合起来就是向公众发出的呼喊。

normal.en: To issue a proclamation is to make a public announcement official.
normal.cn: issue a proclamation 就是把一项公告正式发布出去。

normal.en: A royal proclamation was read aloud in the town square.
normal.cn: 王室公告曾在城镇广场上被大声宣读。

normal.en: The proclamation of independence is a famous historical document.
normal.cn: 独立宣言是一份著名的历史文件。

normal.en: Remember proclaim, exclaim, and clamour share the same root of crying out.
normal.cn: 记住 proclaim、exclaim、clamour 共享「呼喊」这一词根。

normal.en: Compare declaration: a declaration states a position, a proclamation announces it loudly and publicly.
normal.cn: 对比 declaration：declaration 陈述立场，proclamation 则高声公开地宣布。

abstract.en: Picture a herald in a red coat reading a sealed scroll from the steps.
abstract.cn: 想象一名穿红外衣的传令官站在台阶上宣读一卷盖印的文书。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd stopping to listen as one voice carries across the square.
abstract.cn: 想象广场上人群停下脚步，听一个声音传遍全场。

abstract.en: Picture the same words later nailed to a wooden door for everyone to read.
abstract.cn: 想象同一段话后来被钉在木门上，供所有人阅读。

examples.en: The king issued a proclamation banning any further hunting in the royal forest.
examples.cn: 国王发布公告，禁止在王林中继续狩猎。

examples.en: After the election, the proclamation of the result took place on the town hall steps.
examples.cn: 选举之后，结果的宣布在市政厅台阶上进行。

examples.en: Her sudden resignation was a proclamation that she no longer trusted the board.
examples.cn: 她的突然辞职是一种公开表明：她已不再信任董事会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑克来妹神」——拿着扑克牌到广场来，像女神般大声宣布；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、当众）+ clamare（呼喊）→ proclamare（当众喊出）→ proclamatio → 古法语 proclamacion → 英语 proclamation，核心义「当众喊出、让所有人知道」。

sensesIntro.en: Proclamation starts as words cried out to the public, then becomes the act of announcing, the written document, any open personal declaration, and finally a sports call.
sensesIntro.cn: proclamation 先指当众喊给公众听的话，再指宣布这一行为，接着指书面文书，又扩展到个人公开表明，最后进入体育比赛的宣告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an official standing on a platform shouting a sealed notice to the crowd.
core.cn: 核心意象：官员站在高台上，向人群高声宣读一份盖印的文告。

branches.en: The official public announcement is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 官方公告是最日常的义项。

branches.en: The act of announcing focuses on the event rather than the text.
branches.cn: 宣告这一行为关注的是事件本身，而非文本。

branches.en: The sealed document is the shout fixed on paper.
branches.cn: 盖印文书就是被固定在纸上的那声呼喊。

branches.en: Both official and personal declarations send a message into public view.
branches.cn: 官方与个人的表明都是把信息送入公众视野。

branches.en: Rulers and umpires both use the word to make a new state known to everyone.
branches.cn: 统治者和裁判都用这个词向所有人告知一种新状态。

intro.en: Proclamation is built on the Latin root clam-, with pro- and -ation shaping it into a public noun.
intro.cn: proclamation 建在拉丁词根 clam-（呼喊）之上，由前缀 pro- 与词尾 -ation 塑造成表示「公开」的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin clamare means to cry out, and proclamare means to cry out in public.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 clamare 意为呼喊，proclamare 意为当众喊出。

items.meaning: forth, in front of, in public
items.example: Pro- sends the cry forward into the open.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 把这声呼喊推向前方、推向公开。

items.example: The root clam- carries the idea of a loud voice.
items.exampleCN: 词根 clam- 携带「大声」这一概念。

items.example: Clamare is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: clamare 是这整个词族的源头动词。

items.example: Proclamare joins pro- with clamare.
items.exampleCN: proclamare 是 pro- 与 clamare 的结合。

items.example: Proclamatio is the Latin noun of the act.
items.exampleCN: proclamatio 是表示该行为的拉丁名词。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms proclamation from a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 把动词变成 proclamation。

items.example: Exclaim uses the same root with ex- for out.
items.exampleCN: exclaim 用同一个词根，前缀 ex- 表示向外。

items.example: Clamour keeps the noise of the root.
items.exampleCN: clamour 保留了词根的「嘈杂」意味。

items.example: Proclaim is the verb that proclamation comes from.
items.exampleCN: proclaim 是 proclamation 所由而来的动词。

definition_zh: 拖延；耽搁；拖到明天；迟迟不做
definition_en: to delay doing something that should be done, often until it is too late or until the last moment
core_image: 桌上摊着作业，人却把椅子往后挪，一直推到明天
scene: 明天就要交论文，可学生还在反复刷手机。He tends to procrastinate whenever a deadline feels far away.
sceneCN: 这里 procrastinate 是「拖延」（第 1 个义项：该做的事迟迟不做，往后推）；句意：只要截止日期感觉还远，他就容易拖延。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ion 构成，义为「拖延；拖拉」
动词加 -or 构成，表示「习惯拖延的人」
倾向于拖延的，动词加 -ive 表性质

senses.title: To delay what should be done
senses.definition: to keep putting off a task that you know you ought to do, usually replacing it with something easier
senses.definitionCN: 一直推迟明知该做的事情，通常拿更轻松的事来代替
senses.example: I always procrastinate when the assignment is long and boring.
senses.exampleCN: 作业一长一枯燥，我总会拖延。
senses.why: The Latin root cras means tomorrow, so to procrastinate is to keep moving a duty into a tomorrow that never arrives.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 cras 意为「明天」，所以拖延就是不断把责任挪向一个永远不来的明天。

senses.title: To delay until the deadline
senses.titleCN: 拖到期限临近；拖沓误事
senses.definition: to postpone action so long that the time left becomes very short, often leading to hurry or failure
senses.definitionCN: 把行动推迟过久，以致剩下的时间极少，往往导致仓促或失败
senses.example: The committee procrastinated until the report was due the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会一直拖到报告第二天早上要交时才开始动手。
senses.why: Piling up tomorrows on top of each other eats the calendar, so the core image shows up as a last-minute rush.
senses.whyCN: 一个又一个「明天」层层堆叠，把日历啃光，于是核心意象就表现为最后一刻的慌乱赶工。

senses.title: To delay a decision
senses.definition: to avoid making a choice or giving an answer, hoping that time itself will settle the matter
senses.definitionCN: 回避作出选择或给出答复，指望时间自己把事情解决
senses.example: He procrastinates over every job offer and ends up with none.
senses.exampleCN: 他在每个工作机会上都拖延不决，最后什么都没拿到。
senses.why: The postponed thing need not be a task: a decision can also be pushed to tomorrow, which is the abstract face of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 被推后的不必是任务，一个决定同样能被推到明天，这是同一意象的抽象一面。

senses.title: In technical writing
senses.definition: to postpone something formally, especially in older legal or scientific texts where the word is nearly neutral
senses.definitionCN: 正式地把某事推迟，尤其见于较早的法律或科学文本，此时该词几乎不带贬义
senses.example: The court may procrastinate the hearing if new evidence appears.
senses.exampleCN: 如果出现新证据，法院可以推迟听证。
senses.why: The Latin pro- means forward and cras means tomorrow, so the neutral sense is only an official way of saying put it off until tomorrow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 pro- 表示向前，cras 表示明天，因而这个中性义项只是把「推到明天」说得正式一些。

senses.title: In psychology
senses.definition: the studied habit of avoiding a task despite expecting to pay a price for the delay
senses.definitionCN: 心理学研究的习惯性回避任务行为，尽管知道拖延会带来代价
senses.example: Researchers measure how students procrastinate under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者测量学生在压力下如何拖延。
senses.why: Once the habit is named and measured, the everyday image becomes a research topic with causes such as anxiety and poor planning.
senses.whyCN: 当这种习惯被命名并量化，日常画面就变成研究课题，原因涉及焦虑与计划能力不足。

intro.en: Procrastinate is built from Latin pro- (forward), cras (tomorrow), and the suffix -inate, so it literally means to move something forward to tomorrow.
intro.cn: procrastinate 由拉丁语 pro-（向前）、cras（明天）与词尾 -inate 构成，字面意思就是「把某事推到明天」。

items.en: Cras means tomorrow, the day that keeps arriving and is never today.
items.cn: cras 意为明天，一个总会到来却永远不是今天的日子。

items.en: Procrastinare is a rare late Latin verb meaning to put off until tomorrow.
items.cn: procrastinare 是较晚出现的拉丁语动词，意为推迟到明天。

items.en: The suffix -are marks the infinitive, giving pro- plus crastinus plus -are.
items.cn: 词尾 -are 是动词不定式标记，构成「向前 + 明天的 + -are」的组合。

items.en: The verb enters English as a slightly formal word for postponing.
items.cn: 该动词进入英语，作为略正式的表达，指推迟。

items.en: Modern English gives it a moral tone and makes procrastination a subject of psychology.
items.cn: 现代英语赋予它道德色彩，并让「拖延」成为心理学题目。

note.en: Procrastinate shares the cras root with the old word procrastination, and it sits beside other verbs about delay.
note.cn: procrastinate 与旧词形彼此同根，都含 cras（明天）意；它也与表示耽搁的其他动词相邻。

entries.definition: the habit of delaying tasks that need doing
to produce young, from a different Latin root
entries.definitionCN: 生育后代，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: lying flat on the ground, from a different root
entries.definitionCN: 俯卧的，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to move an event to a later time on purpose
to make something happen later than planned
to waste time by moving slowly

normalIntro.en: Procrastinate has tomorrow built into it: pro- forward, cras tomorrow, so the whole word is a duty pushed forward to the next day.
normalIntro.cn: procrastinate 自带「明天」：pro- 向前，cras 明天，整个词就是把责任向前推到下一天。

normal.en: Procrastination is the noun, procrastinator the person who always delays.
normal.cn: procrastination 是名词，procrastinator 指总爱拖延的人。

normal.en: To procrastinate on a task means to keep leaving it for tomorrow.
normal.cn: procrastinate on a task 指一直把任务留到明天。

normal.en: Students who procrastinate often work all night before a deadline.
normal.cn: 有拖延习惯的学生常在截止前熬个通宵。

normal.en: Compare postpone: postpone moves a plan on purpose, procrastinate usually implies a fault.
normal.cn: 对比 postpone：postpone 是有意改期，procrastinate 通常带有过失意味。

normal.en: The word is nearly always negative in modern use, so it pairs well with guilt, stress, and deadlines.
normal.cn: 现代用法中该词几乎总是贬义，因此常与内疚、压力和截止日期连用。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of little notes each marked tomorrow, growing taller on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上堆起一叠小纸条，每张都写着「明天」，越堆越高。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands keep sliding back while you clean your desk instead.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表的指针不断往回滑，而你却在擦桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a decision left on a shelf, gathering dust because nobody will pick it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一个决定被搁在架子上积灰，因为没人愿意把它拿下来。

examples.en: If you procrastinate again, you will miss the scholarship deadline.
examples.cn: 你要是再拖延，就会错过奖学金截止日期。

examples.en: She procrastinated for weeks before finally calling the landlord.
examples.cn: 她拖了好几周才终于给房东打电话。

examples.en: A simple plan can help you stop procrastinating in the evening.
examples.cn: 一个简单的计划能帮你在晚上不再拖延。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑罗·克拉斯廷内特」——听起来像「拖着菜刀慢慢来」，刀都磨钝了活儿还没动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ cras（明天）+ 动词词尾 → procrastinare（推到明天）→ 英语 procrastinate，核心义「把该做的事往后推到明天」。

sensesIntro.en: Procrastinate begins with putting off a duty, deepens into last-minute delay and indecision, and widens into a neutral technical use and a studied psychological habit.
sensesIntro.cn: procrastinate 先从推迟职责说起，再深化为临期拖延和迟迟不决，最后扩展到中性的技术用法和被研究的心理习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a duty nudged forward one more day, again and again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份责任被一次次向前挪一天。

branches.en: Putting off a task is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 推迟任务是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Endless tomorrows shrink the remaining time to the last moment.
branches.cn: 无数个明天把剩余时间压缩到最后一刻。

branches.en: A decision can be postponed just like a task.
branches.cn: 决定和任务一样可以被推迟。

branches.en: Formal postponing and last-minute delaying share the same push forward in time.
branches.cn: 正式的推迟与临期拖延共享同一种「在时间上后移」的动作。

branches.en: Psychology turns the everyday habit into measurable behaviour.
branches.cn: 心理学把日常习惯变成可测量的行为。

intro.en: Procrastinate is a Latin compound: pro- sends things forward, and cras (tomorrow) supplies the time word at its heart.
intro.cn: procrastinate 是拉丁语复合词：pro- 表示向前推，词心是表示时间的 cras（明天）。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- means forward, cras means tomorrow, and -are marks the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pro- 意为向前，cras 意为明天，-are 是动词词尾。

items.example: The prefix pro- moves the deed forward in time.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 让事情在时间上向前挪。

items.example: Cras is the time word hidden inside the verb.
items.exampleCN: cras 是藏在动词里的时间词。

items.example: Crastinus turns the adverb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: crastinus 把副词变成形容词。

items.example: Procrastinare is the direct Latin ancestor.
items.exampleCN: procrastinare 是直接的拉丁祖先。

items.example: The ending -are marks the first conjugation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -are 标记第一变位法动词。

items.meaning: forming a verb from a Latin stem
items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词干构成动词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate turns the stem into procrastinate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把词干变成 procrastinate。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing something
items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms procrastination.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 procrastination。

items.example: The suffix -or forms procrastinator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 procrastinator。

items.example: Procrastination names the habit itself.
items.exampleCN: procrastination 命名这一习惯本身。

definition_zh: 获得；取得；采购；设法取得；筹得
definition_en: to obtain something that is needed, often after effort or through an official process, with or without payment
core_image: 一个人走过长长的走廊，把批好的领料单换成手里的一箱物资
scene: 医院物资告急，采购员连夜打电话联系供应商。The hospital had to procure enough masks before the winter wave arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 procure 是「采购；设法取得」（第 2 个义项：通过购买或官方渠道得到所需之物）；句意：医院必须在冬季疫情高峰到来前采购到足够的口罩。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ment 构成，义为「采购；取得（的过程）」
动词加 -able 构成，义为「可获得的；可取得的」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「取得者；采办人」

senses.title: To obtain with effort
senses.definition: to get something that is hard to find or that requires effort, by asking, searching, or working for it
senses.definitionCN: 通过询问、寻找或努力，得到难以找到或需要付出力气的东西
senses.example: She finally procured a copy of the out-of-print novel for the library.
senses.exampleCN: 她终于为图书馆弄到了一本绝版小说。
senses.why: The Latin verb procurare meant to take care of or look after a matter, so getting something means you have attended to it until it is in your hands.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「照料、经办」，所以把东西弄到手，意味着你一路照应、操办，直到它真正落在你手里。

senses.title: To buy or obtain supplies
senses.definition: to obtain goods, materials, or services for an organisation, usually through a formal order or purchase
senses.definitionCN: 为机构通过正式订单或购买取得货物、材料或服务
senses.example: The school procures all its paper from a single local supplier.
senses.exampleCN: 学校所有纸张都从本地一家供应商采购。
senses.why: In offices and hospitals the cared-for matter becomes stock, so the verb settles into the buying sense.
senses.whyCN: 在机关和医院里，被办妥的「事」变成了库存，于是这个动词固定为「采购」义。

senses.title: To arrange for someone or something
senses.definition: to arrange for a person, service, or solution to be provided, often after a search
senses.definitionCN: 经过一番寻找后安排好人手、服务或解决办法
senses.example: They procured a translator at short notice.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在短时间内找来了一位译员。
senses.why: Because procuration meant looking after another person, the verb can also mean obtaining people and their help.
senses.whyCN: 因为拉丁语名词有「替人办事」的含义，这个动词也能表示弄到人手及其帮助。

senses.title: To bring about a result
senses.definition: to cause a result to happen, especially in older literary use where people procure peace, honour, or ruin
senses.definitionCN: 使某种结果发生，尤见于较早的文学用法，如促成和平、荣誉或毁败
senses.example: Patient talks procured peace between the two camps.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心的谈判促成了两个阵营之间的和平。
senses.why: If the cared-for matter is an outcome, then tending to it amounts to making that outcome happen.
senses.whyCN: 如果被照料的「事」是一种结果，那么一路操心操办，就等于让这个结果发生。

senses.title: To obtain a person for sex work
senses.definition: to find and bring a person to take part in prostitution, a crime in most legal systems
senses.definitionCN: 寻找并带来某人从事卖淫，在多数法律体系中都属犯罪
senses.example: He was charged with procuring for a group of hotels.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控为一组酒店拉客卖淫。
