senses.why: The neutral core of obtaining people is pushed to its dark extreme: procurer became the legal name for one who supplies others for payment.
senses.whyCN: 「弄到人手」的中性核心被推到黑暗极端：procurer 成了法律上给他人提供卖淫者的称呼。

intro.en: Procure comes from Latin procurare, to attend to or look after a matter, built on pro- and curare, to care for.
intro.cn: procure 来自拉丁语 procurare（照料、经办某事），由 pro- 与 curare（关心、照料）构成。

items.en: Cura means care or concern, and curare means to look after.
items.cn: cura 意为关心、照料，curare 意为照管。

items.en: Procurare means to look after a matter, often on behalf of another person.
items.cn: procurare 意为操办某事，常是替他人经办。

items.en: Procurator is the Latin name for an agent trusted to look after business.
items.cn: procurator 是拉丁语中受委托经办事务之代理人的称呼。

items.en: The Old French verb procurer carries the same sense of managing and getting things done.
items.cn: 古法语动词 procurer 同样带有经办、把事情办成的意思。

items.en: The word enters English as a legal term for acting as an agent, before it comes to mean to obtain.
items.cn: 该词进入英语时先是法律术语，指充当代理人，后来才表示「获得」。

items.en: Modern English focuses on obtaining supplies, and the buying sense becomes common in business.
items.cn: 现代英语侧重获取物资，购买义在商业中变得常见。

note.en: Procure is the English form of Latin procurare, sharing the cura root with cure and curator, and it stands beside other verbs for getting things.
note.cn: procure 是拉丁语 procurare 的英语形式，与 cure、curator 共享 cura 词根，并与表示「取得」的其他动词相邻。

entries.definition: the process of obtaining supplies for an organisation
to make a person well again
a person who looks after a collection or museum
entries.definitionCN: 馆藏负责人，同源于「照料」

entries.definition: to get something, especially by making an effort
to get or gain something over time
to buy something with money

normalIntro.en: Procure carries the cura root of care: you procure what you look after until it is safely in your hands.
normalIntro.cn: procure 带着 cura（关心照料）这一词根：你把事情照看到底，东西才稳妥地落到手里。

normal.en: Procurement is the noun for the buying process, procurable the adjective for goods you can get.
normal.cn: procurement 是采购流程的名词，procurable 表示「可获得的」。

normal.en: To procure funding is to get the money a project needs.
normal.cn: procure funding 就是为项目筹到所需资金。

normal.en: Companies procure supplies through contracts, not casual shopping.
normal.cn: 企业是通过合同采购物资的，而不是随手购物。

normal.en: Compare obtain and acquire: procure is more formal and often suggests effort or official channels.
normal.cn: 对比 obtain 和 acquire：procure 更正式，常暗示费力或通过正式渠道。

normal.en: Remember cure and curator: all three words start from curing, meaning caring.
normal.cn: 记住 cure 和 curator：三个词都源于 curare，表示「照料」。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor walked at last to the supply room door, and the order finally signed.
abstract.cn: 想象走过一条长长的走廊，终于来到库房门口，单据也终于签好。

abstract.en: Imagine a list of missing items slowly being ticked off one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张缺货清单被一项一项划掉。

abstract.en: Picture a committee meeting that finally ends in a decision to act.
abstract.cn: 想象会议终于结束，并作出采取行动的决定。

examples.en: The team managed to procure rare seeds from a distant botanical garden.
examples.cn: 团队设法从远方的植物园弄到了稀有种子。

examples.en: Every item procured for the project must be recorded in a public log.
examples.cn: 为该项目采购的每一件物品都必须记入公开日志。

examples.en: Without a guarantor, it is almost impossible to procure a loan from that bank.
examples.cn: 没有担保人，几乎不可能从那家银行获得贷款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑罗·求尔」——拼命去「求」你，东西才拿到手；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、代为）+ cura（关心、照料，curare 照料）→ procurare（操办、经办）→ 古法语 procurer → 英语 procure，核心义「一路操办，最终弄到手」。

sensesIntro.en: Procure starts from caring for a matter until something is obtained, then narrows into buying supplies, extends to arranging people and outcomes, and finally occurs in a legal sense about sex work.
sensesIntro.cn: procure 由照料一件事直到把东西弄到手说起，再收窄为采购物资，又扩展到安排人手与促成结果，最后出现在关于卖淫的法律义项中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an agent walking to the supply desk with a signed order until the goods are in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：代理人拿着签字单据走到窗口，直到物资到手为止。

branches.en: Obtaining with effort is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 费力取得是最日常的义项。

branches.en: Buying supplies is obtaining formalised into business routine.
branches.cn: 采购是把取得固化为商业流程。

branches.en: Arranging people and services is obtaining beyond objects.
branches.cn: 安排人手与服务是超出物品范围的取得。

branches.en: An outcome can be cared for into existence like a thing.
branches.cn: 结果也像物品一样被操心操办出来。

branches.en: The legal sense turns obtaining a person into a criminal act.
branches.cn: 法律义项把人当作「取得」的对象，使之为犯罪。

intro.en: Procure is built on Latin procurare, where pro- (on behalf of) joins cura, care, and gives English the family of cure, curator, and procurement.
intro.cn: procure 建基于拉丁语 procurare，前缀 pro-（代为）与 cura（照料）结合，为英语带来 cure、curator、procurement 这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura means care, and procurare means to see to a matter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 意为照料，procurare 意为经办某事。

items.example: Pro- gives the sense of acting for another person.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 带来「替他人办事」的意思。

items.example: The root cur- runs through the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词根 cur- 贯穿整个词族。

items.example: Cura is the heart of the verb.
items.exampleCN: cura 是这个词的动词核心。

items.meaning: to look after, to attend to
items.example: Curare is the caring verb behind cure.
items.exampleCN: curare 是 cure 背后的「照料」动词。

items.example: Procurare supplies the English stem.
items.exampleCN: procurare 提供英语词干。

items.meaning: an agent, one trusted to act
items.example: Procurator names the person who acts for another.
items.exampleCN: procurator 指替他人办事的人。

items.example: Procure shortens the Latin verb into English.
items.exampleCN: procure 把拉丁动词缩短成英语词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms procurement.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 procurement。

items.example: The suffix -able forms procurable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 procurable。

items.example: Curator keeps the meaning of looking after.
items.exampleCN: curator 保留了「照管」的含义。

definition_zh: 巨大的；惊人的；庞大的；异常的；才华出众的
definition_en: extremely large, great, or unusual in amount, size, or quality, so that it seems astonishing
core_image: 一头巨鲸浮出海面，脊背像一座移动的小岛
scene: 老渔夫谈起年轻时在海上遇见的那头鲸，说它的背几乎比整条船还宽。The old sailor described the whale as a prodigious creature that could swallow three boats at once.
sceneCN: 这里 prodigious 是「巨大的、惊人的」（第 1 个义项：尺寸或数量大到令人惊异）；句意：老水手形容那头鲸是个庞然巨物，一口能吞下三条船。

pos.zh: 巨大的；惊人的；异常的；才华出众的

derivatives.zh: 由 prodigious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「惊人地；巨大地」
由 prodigious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「巨大；惊人；非凡」
同根名词，义为「奇才；神童；奇迹」，由拉丁语 prodigium 直接演变而来

senses.title: Astonishingly large in size or amount
senses.definition: extremely great in size, amount, or degree, so great that it surprises or overwhelms
senses.definitionCN: 在体积、数量或程度上极大，大到令人吃惊或难以承受
senses.example: The expedition needed a prodigious amount of food and fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟远征需要惊人多的食物和燃料。
senses.why: Prodigious comes from Latin prodigium, a portent or monstrous omen; anything of omen-like scale is prodigious.
senses.whyCN: prodigious 来自拉丁语 prodigium（预兆、异象怪物）；凡是像异象那样巨大、超出常理的东西，就用这个词。

senses.title: Extraordinary in degree or power
senses.definition: very great or extreme in force, ability, or intensity, often used with admiration
senses.definitionCN: 在力量、能力或强度上非常突出或极端，常带赞叹意味
senses.example: She has a prodigious memory for names and dates.
senses.exampleCN: 她对名字和日期有惊人的记忆力。
senses.why: The same omen image is applied to quality rather than size: a talent that exceeds the ordinary as a portent exceeds nature.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「异象」意象被用到品质而非体积上：一种才华超出常规，就像异象超出自然常理。

senses.title: Causing wonder or amazement
senses.definition: arousing wonder or amazement because of its scale or strangeness
senses.definitionCN: 因规模或奇特而引人惊叹、令人称奇
senses.example: From the cliff the falls looked absolutely prodigious.
senses.exampleCN: 从悬崖上看，那瀑布壮观得令人惊叹。
senses.why: A prodigium was a sign that made people stop and stare; the word keeps that response of astonishment.
senses.whyCN: prodigium 是让人驻足凝望的征兆；这个词保留了那种「令人惊叹」的反应。

senses.title: Phenomenal effort or work
senses.definition: used of effort, work, or output that is enormous and hard to match
senses.definitionCN: 形容努力、工作或产量极大，难以企及
senses.example: Finishing the bridge in two years took prodigious effort from the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 在两年内建成这座桥，全镇付出了巨大的努力。
senses.why: Effort measured on a monstrous scale: the work is so large that it seems almost beyond human proportion.
senses.whyCN: 努力被放在异乎寻常的尺度上衡量：工作量之大，几乎超出了人的常态。

intro.en: Prodigious comes from Latin prodigium, a portent or monstrous sign, by way of the adjective prodigiosus.
intro.cn: prodigious 经形容词 prodigiosus 来自拉丁语 prodigium（预兆、异象），词义从「像征兆一样离奇」逐渐转向「巨大、惊人」。

items.en: Prodigium meant a sign, omen, or unnatural event, and also a monster or monstrosity.
items.cn: prodigium 指征兆、异象或违背自然的事件，也指怪物、怪胎。

items.en: The adjective prodigiosus described something omen-like, wonderful, or unnatural.
items.cn: 形容词 prodigiosus 形容像征兆一般、奇妙或反常的事物。

items.en: Renaissance Latin revived prodigiosus with the sense of extraordinary, amazing.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的拉丁语重新启用 prodigiosus，义为「非凡的、惊人的」。

items.en: English adopts prodigious in the sixteenth century, first meaning strange or portentous, then huge and wonderful.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 prodigious，最初意为「奇怪的、预示性的」，后来转为「巨大的、奇妙的」。

items.en: By the nineteenth century prodigious is chiefly a word for enormous size, strength, or ability.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，prodigious 主要用来形容巨大的规模、力量或能力。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the prodig- root and its omen idea; the near-meaning group gathers other words for very great size.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 prodig- 词根及其「异象」意象；近义组收其他表示「极大」的词。

entries.definition: a young person with exceptional talent, or a wonderful or strange thing
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神童、奇才、奇迹」，与 prodigious 同出拉丁语 prodigium。

entries.definition: an adverb meaning to an astonishing degree
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「惊人地、巨大地」，由 prodigious 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: the habit of wasting money or resources carelessly; it comes from prodigal, not from prodigium
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挥霍、浪费」；来自 prodigal，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: very large in size or amount; plainer and more neutral than prodigious
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，比 prodigious 更平实中性。

entries.definition: extremely large or vast, especially in a way that fills the view or the mind
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「广大的、无限的」，强调辽阔无边。

entries.definition: remarkable or extraordinary, often in results or performance
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非凡的、显著的」，多用于成绩或表现。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root prodigium and the phrases prodigious actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 prodigium，以及 prodigious 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Prodigium is a portent or monster; prodigious describes anything of that unnatural scale.
normal.cn: prodigium 是预兆或怪物；prodigious 形容那种超出常态的规模。

normal.en: Prodigy and prodigious share the root: a wonder in a person, a wonder in size.
normal.cn: prodigy 与 prodigious 同根：一个是人的奇迹，一个是大小的奇迹。

normal.en: A prodigious memory or appetite is a way of praising what is beyond the ordinary.
normal.cn: prodigious memory 或 prodigious appetite 都是在赞叹超出常规之处。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with prodigal, which means wasteful rather than huge.
normal.cn: 不要混同 prodigal，那是「挥霍的、浪费的」，而不是「巨大的」。

normal.en: In essays, use prodigious mainly with amounts, effort, talent, or energy.
normal.cn: 在作文里，prodigious 多搭配数量、努力、天赋或精力。

abstract.en: Picture a whale surfacing beside a small boat until the boat looks like a toy.
abstract.cn: 想象一头鲸在小船旁浮出水面，直到小船看起来像个玩具。

abstract.en: Imagine a tide pulling a stone tower until it leans: the force is prodigious.
abstract.cn: 想象一股潮水把石塔拉得倾斜：那股力量就是 prodigious 的惊人之力。

abstract.en: Think of an old sign in the sky that makes the whole village stop and stare.
abstract.cn: 想象天空中一道古老的异象，让整个村子停下脚步凝望。

examples.en: The library holds a prodigious collection of old maps.
examples.cn: 这座图书馆藏有数量惊人的古地图。

examples.en: He built the shed with prodigious effort and very little help.
examples.cn: 他凭巨大的努力、几乎无人帮忙建起了这间棚屋。

examples.en: Even by local standards, the harvest was prodigious.
examples.cn: 即便按当地的尺度衡量，这次收成也大得惊人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普罗迪句斯」——仿佛有人赞叹：普罗大众都惊呆了，这尺寸太惊人；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prodigium「预兆、异象；怪物」→ prodigiosus「像征兆的、非凡的」→ 英语 prodigious，核心义由「离奇得像异象」转向「巨大得惊人」。同根词 prodigy（奇才、奇迹）。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of prodigious grow from one image of an omen-sized thing: sheer size, extraordinary quality, the wonder it causes, and the effort it demands.
sensesIntro.cn: prodigious 的四个义项都长自同一个「异象般的事物」意象：体积之大、品质之非凡、它所引起的惊叹，以及它所要求的巨大努力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whale surfacing beside a small boat, its back like a moving island.
core.cn: 核心意象：巨鲸在小船旁浮出海面，脊背像一座移动的岛。

branches.en: SIZE: amounts and spaces that exceed ordinary measure.
branches.cn: 规模线：超出常规尺度的数量与空间。

branches.en: QUALITY: ability, force, or memory that is beyond the ordinary.
branches.cn: 品质线：超出常规的才能、力量或记忆。

branches.en: RESPONSE: the wonder or awe the thing produces.
branches.cn: 反应线：事物引起的惊叹与敬畏。

branches.en: WORK: effort and output measured on the same enormous scale.
branches.cn: 劳作线：努力与产出也按同样的巨大尺度来衡量。

branches.en: Size and ability share the same root idea of going beyond natural proportion.
branches.cn: 规模与能力共享同一个「超出自然比例」的词根理念。

intro.en: Prodigious is built from the Latin noun prodigium plus the adjective suffix -ous, and English adds -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: prodigious 由拉丁语名词 prodigium 加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，英语再用 -ly 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin prodigium, prodigiosus and the related noun prodigium-family forms are recorded; only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prodigium、prodigiosus 均有文献记录，只有更早的词源属于推测。

items.example: The prefix marks something that comes before as a sign.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分表示「事先来到」以示征兆。

items.example: Prodigium is the source noun.
items.exampleCN: prodigium 是来源名词。

items.example: Prodigiosus is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: prodigiosus 是直接前身。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous carries the Latin ending into English.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 把拉丁语词尾带入英语。

items.example: Prodigious keeps the omen sense of scale.
items.exampleCN: prodigious 保留了预兆般的规模感。

items.example: It forms prodigiously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prodigiously。

items.example: It forms prodigiousness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 prodigiousness。

items.example: Prodigy keeps the noun sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: prodigy 保留了词根的名词义。

items.example: The -ig- survives in prodig- words.
items.exampleCN: prodig- 系列词保留了 -ig-。

definition_zh: 亵渎；玷污；世俗的；亵渎的；粗俗的
definition_en: to treat something sacred with disrespect, or describing words and things that are not sacred or that offend religious feeling
core_image: 一只沾满泥土的手伸进圣坛前洁净的围栏里
scene: 游客的鞋踩上了古老的圣坛台阶，还被管理员大声制止。A tourist was told off for shouting profane jokes inside the quiet chapel.
sceneCN: 这里 profane 是「亵渎的、不敬的」（第 4 个义项：言语或行为对神圣之物失敬）；句意：一名游客在安静的礼拜堂里讲亵渎的玩笑，被管理员训斥了。

pos.zh: 亵渎；玷污；滥用（神圣之物）

derivatives.zh: 由 profane 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「亵渎；脏话；粗俗语言」
由 profane 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「亵渎地；粗俗地」
由拉丁语 profanare 演变而来，义为「亵渎神圣之物的行为」
由 profane 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「亵渎性；世俗性」

senses.title: Not sacred; belonging to ordinary life
senses.definition: not holy or religious, belonging to the everyday world outside a temple or church
senses.definitionCN: 不神圣、不属宗教的，属于神庙或教堂之外日常生活世界的
senses.example: The rule forbids music in that holy place, but profane songs are fine outside.
senses.exampleCN: 那条规矩禁止在这处圣所里奏乐，但在外面唱世俗歌曲无妨。
senses.why: Latin profanus meant outside the temple, from pro- before plus fanum shrine, so the word first names the space outside holy ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 profanus 意为「神庙之外的」，由 pro-（在……之前）加 fanum（圣所）构成，因此这个词最初指的是神圣场地之外的空间。

senses.title: To treat sacred things with disrespect
senses.definition: to treat a sacred place, object, or belief with contempt or careless violation
senses.definitionCN: 以轻蔑或随意的侵害对待神圣的场所、物品或信仰
senses.example: Graffiti artists profaned the walls of the old monastery.
senses.exampleCN: 涂鸦者玷污了那座古老修道院的墙壁。
senses.why: What is placed outside the shrine is what has lost its sanctity; the verb describes dragging holy things into ordinary, careless use.
senses.whyCN: 被放到圣所之外，就等于失去了神圣性；动词义正描述把神圣之物拖进日常随意的使用之中。

senses.title: To misuse something sacred or respected
senses.definition: to put a sacred or highly respected thing to an unworthy or common use
senses.definitionCN: 把神圣或极受尊敬的事物用于不值得、普通的用途
senses.example: Critics said the company profaned the national anthem in an advert.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说这家公司在广告里滥用了国歌。
senses.why: The shrine image extends to anything held sacred in a culture, such as a flag, an anthem, or a memorial.
senses.whyCN: 圣所的意象被扩展到文化中被视为神圣的事物，如国旗、国歌或纪念碑。

senses.title: Speaking or acting in an irreverent way
senses.definition: used of words, jokes, or behaviour that show contempt for religion or holy things
senses.definitionCN: 形容言语、玩笑或行为对宗教或圣物表现出轻蔑
senses.example: His profane remarks in the chapel shocked the visiting school group.
senses.exampleCN: 他在礼拜堂里说的亵渎之语让来访的学生团体大为震惊。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the outside-the-shrine border and marks speech that has crossed it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「圣所之外」的界线，并标记出越过这条界线的言语。

senses.title: Crude or offensive language
senses.definition: describing coarse, vulgar language, especially swearing and cursing
senses.definitionCN: 形容粗俗、下流的话，尤指咒骂与脏话
senses.example: The referee booked him for profane abuse towards the line judge.
senses.exampleCN: 他因对边裁讲粗话辱骂而被裁判出示黄牌。
senses.why: The border between holy and ordinary shifted again: ordinary speech became marked as the speech unfit for sacred ears.
senses.whyCN: 神圣与平常之间的界线再次移动：「平常的话」被标记为不适合圣洁之耳的话，于是转为「粗俗之语」。

senses.title: The profane as an abstract category
senses.definition: in religious studies, the category of ordinary, non-sacred reality as opposed to the sacred
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教学中，与「神圣」相对的普通、非神圣现实的范畴
senses.example: The anthropologist studied how the sacred and the profane divide space in village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位人类学家研究村庄生活中神圣与世俗如何划分空间。
senses.why: A descriptive noun use turns the old temple boundary into a general concept used by scholars.
senses.whyCN: 描述性的名词用法把古老的圣所界线变成学者使用的一般概念。

intro.en: Profane comes from Latin profanus, meaning outside the shrine, and passes through Old French into English.
intro.cn: profane 来自拉丁语 profanus（圣所之外的），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Fanum meant a shrine or temple, and pro- meant before or outside, so profanus described a person or place outside the sacred enclosure.
items.cn: fanum 指圣所或神庙，pro- 表示「在……之前／之外」，因此 profanus 描述圣所以外的地点或人。

items.en: One etymology links fanum to fari, to speak, through the idea of a place declared sacred, but this connection is generally accepted rather than certain.
items.cn: 有一种词源说认为 fanum 与 fari（说话）有关，指「被宣告为神圣之地」；这一联系一般认为成立，但并非定论。

items.en: The verb profanare meant to desecrate, and it supplies the English verb sense.
items.cn: 动词 profanare 意为「亵渎」，为英语的动词义提供了来源。

items.en: Old French profane carried the adjective and the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 profane 把形容词与动词形式带入英语。

items.en: English records the adjective in the fourteenth century and the verb a little later; exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录到形容词，动词稍晚出现；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Later uses extend from desecrating a temple to crude language and to the scholarly opposition of sacred and profane.
items.cn: 后来的用法从亵渎神庙扩展到粗俗语言，以及学术上「神圣与世俗」的对立。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the profan- family and the fanum root; the near-meaning group gathers other words about violating or despising the sacred.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 profan- 词族与 fanum 词根；近义组收其他表示「侵犯、蔑视神圣」的词。

entries.definition: the noun for profane language or the act of showing contempt for the sacred
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「亵渎、脏话」，由 profane 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: an adverb meaning in a profane or irreverent way
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「亵渎地、粗俗地」。

entries.definition: the act of treating sacred things with disrespect
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「亵渎行为」，源自拉丁语 profanare。

entries.definition: very deep, or showing deep understanding; it merely shares the pro- prefix
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深刻的、深远的」；只是共享 pro- 前缀，拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: holy and deserving reverence, the direct opposite of profane
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「神圣的」，是 profane 的直接反义词。

entries.definition: not connected with religion, said of laws, schools, or institutions in a neutral way
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「世俗的、非宗教的」，语气中性，多指制度、法律。

entries.definition: to violate or damage something sacred, usually a place or object
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「玷污、亵渎」，多指圣地或圣物。

entries.definition: rude, coarse, or in bad taste, without the religious dimension
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「粗俗的、下流的」，不带宗教色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks rest on the real Latin boundary pro- plus fanum, the shrine, and on the phrases the word really takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子建立在真实的拉丁语界线 pro- 加 fanum（圣所）之上，并借用这个词的实际搭配。

normal.en: Pro plus fanum means outside the shrine; profane is whatever stands beyond that holy line.
normal.cn: pro 加 fanum 意为「圣所之外」；profane 就是站在那条神圣界线之外的东西。

normal.en: The noun pair sacred and profane is used together in religious studies.
normal.cn: sacred 与 profane 常作为一对名词，用于宗教学研究。

normal.en: Profanare is the Latin verb that gives the English verb to profane.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 profanare 提供了英语动词 profane 的来源。

normal.en: Profane jokes and profane language mean crude, irreverent speech.
normal.cn: profane jokes 与 profane language 指粗俗、不敬的言语。

normal.en: Do not confuse profane with profound: one is outside the shrine, the other is deep.
normal.cn: 不要混同 profane 与 profound：一个是「在圣所之外」，一个是「深」。

abstract.en: Picture a rope fence round a shrine, and a muddy hand reaching over it.
abstract.cn: 想象神庙外的一圈绳索围栏，一只沾泥的手越过围栏伸了进来。

abstract.en: Imagine the temple door shut, with ordinary street noise and swearing left outside.
abstract.cn: 想象神庙的门关上，普通的街头喧闹与咒骂被留在门外。

abstract.en: Think of an anchor of a flag or an anthem being used to sell soap: something sacred handled as ordinary.
abstract.cn: 想象国旗或国歌被拿去卖肥皂：神圣之物被当作寻常物品处理。

examples.en: He was charged with profaning a protected religious site.
examples.cn: 他被控亵渎一处受保护的宗教场所。

examples.en: The novel mixes sacred and profane themes without irony.
examples.cn: 这部小说毫不反讽地混合了神圣与世俗的主题。

examples.en: Teachers asked the boys to stop using profane words in class.
examples.cn: 老师们要求学生不要在课堂上说粗话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼粪」——把脏东西泼进圣所，就是亵渎；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在……之前、之外）+ fanum（圣所、神庙）→ profanus（圣所之外的、世俗的）→ profanare（亵渎）→ 古法语 profane → 英语 profane；核心义是「越过神圣与世俗的界线」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses of profane all stand on one line between shrine and street: outside the shrine, crossing it, abusing what is inside, and finally speech and studies that mark where the line runs.
sensesIntro.cn: profane 的六个义项都立在圣所与街巷之间的同一条界线上：在界线之外、越过界线、滥用界线内的东西，最后是划出这条界线的言语与学术用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a muddy hand reaching over the rope fence into the shrine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只沾泥的手越过绳索围栏伸进圣所。

branches.en: PLACE: what lies outside the sacred enclosure is ordinary and worldly.
branches.cn: 场所线：圣所围栏之外的东西是普通、世俗的。

branches.en: ACT: crossing the line into the shrine to defile it.
branches.cn: 动作线：越过界线进入圣所将其玷污。

branches.en: MISUSE: sacred things put to unworthy everyday purposes.
branches.cn: 滥用线：把神圣之物用于不配的日常目的。

branches.en: SPEECH: words that cross the line, first irreverent, then simply crude.
branches.cn: 言语线：越过界线的言辞，先是不敬，后来就只是粗俗。

branches.en: CATEGORY: the boundary itself becomes sacred and profane as a pair of scholarly terms.
branches.cn: 范畴线：这条界线本身化为「神圣」与「世俗」一对学术术语。

intro.en: Profane is a Latin compound of pro- before a fanum shrine, with -ous in the Latin adjective and -ity, -ly, -ness in English extensions.
intro.cn: profane 是拉丁语复合词，由 pro- 加 fanum（圣所）构成；后来英语用 -ity、-ly、-ness 等后缀扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fanum, profanus, and profanare are recorded; the link of fanum to fari is generally accepted but not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fanum、profanus 与 profanare 均有文献记录；fanum 与 fari 的联系一般认为成立，但并不确定。

items.example: The prefix places the thing in front of the shrine.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把事物放在圣所之前。

items.example: Fanum is the shrine at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: fanum 是这个词正中的「圣所」。

items.example: Profanus is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: profanus 是形容词的直接来源。

items.example: Profanare gives the English verb sense.
items.exampleCN: profanare 提供了英语动词义。

items.example: Profane keeps the border sense.
items.exampleCN: profane 保留了「界线」的含义。

items.example: It forms profanity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 profanity。

items.example: It forms profanely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 profanely。

items.example: It forms profaneness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 profaneness。

items.example: It forms profanation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 profanation。

definition_zh: 深深地；深切地；极度地；深刻地
definition_en: in a way that is very great, deep, or intense, or in a way that shows deep understanding
core_image: 石头被投进深井，很久才传来一声回响
scene: 老人听完这个年轻人的话，沉默了很久，才轻轻点了点头。The old teacher was profoundly moved by the students who had travelled so far to thank her.
sceneCN: 这里 profoundly 是「深深地、深切地」（第 1 个义项：程度极深，几乎触及内心底部）；句意：那些远道而来向她道谢的学生，让老教师深受感动。

pos.zh: 深深地；深切地；极度地；深刻地

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「深刻的；深远的；深奥的」，profoundly 即其副词形式
由拉丁语 profundus 演变而来，义为「深刻；深奥；深沉」
由 profound 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「深刻；深奥」

senses.title: To a very deep degree
senses.definition: used of feelings or effects that reach far below the surface, so that they are very great and lasting
senses.definitionCN: 用于情感或影响深达表面之下、极其强烈且持久的程度，表示「深深地」
senses.example: She was profoundly touched by the letter from her first student.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一名学生寄来的信让她深受感动。
senses.why: Latin profundus joins pro- forward with fundus bottom, so the word pictures something going all the way down to its base.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 profundus 由 pro-（向前）与 fundus（底部）合成，画面是某物一直抵达最底层。

senses.title: To an extreme degree
senses.definition: used with adjectives to mean very, extremely, often with a contrast in mind
senses.definitionCN: 与形容词连用表示「非常、极度」，常暗含对比
senses.example: The two systems are profoundly different in how they treat privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种制度对待隐私的方式截然不同。
senses.why: Depth becomes a measure of extent: a difference that goes to the bottom of things is extreme.
senses.whyCN: 深度变成了程度的尺度：直达事物底部的差异，也就是极端的差异。

senses.title: With deep insight or thought
senses.definition: in a way that shows deep understanding, serious thought, or insight
senses.definitionCN: 表现出深刻理解、认真思考或洞察力的方式
senses.example: The report comments profoundly on the causes of rural poverty.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告对农村贫困的成因作了深刻的评论。
senses.why: What is deep has its mass hidden below the surface, so a profoundly argued point has more underneath than it shows.
senses.whyCN: 深的东西大部分藏在水面之下，因此「深刻地论述」的观点也是底下比表面更多。

senses.title: In a deep or low physical way
senses.definition: used of low sounds, heavy sleep, or serious conditions such as deafness, where depth is physical
senses.definitionCN: 用于低沉的声音、沉睡或重度失聪等情形，这里的「深」是身体层面的
senses.example: He slept profoundly for twelve hours after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途攀登之后，他沉睡了十二个小时。
senses.why: The original bottom image is still visible: a voice or a sleep is described as reaching down to the fundus.
senses.whyCN: 最原始的「底部」意象仍然可见：声音或睡眠被说成一直沉到最底下。

intro.en: Profoundly is the adverb of profound, which comes from Latin profundus and reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: profoundly 是 profound 的副词形式；profound 来自拉丁语 profundus，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Fundus meant the bottom or base of something, and pro- meant forward or down, so profundus meant deep, bottomless.
items.cn: fundus 指事物的底或基座，pro- 表示「向前、向下」，因此 profundus 意为「深的、无底的」。

items.en: From the physical depth of water came the figurative depth of feeling, thought, and sound.
items.cn: 从水的物理深度，引申出情感、思想与声音层面的「深」。

items.en: Old French profond carried the adjective into English, where it was also spelled profound.
items.cn: 古法语 profond 把形容词带入英语，英语中拼作 profound。

items.en: The adjective is recorded from the fourteenth century; the adverb -ly form follows it closely.
items.cn: 形容词在十四世纪有记录；副词 -ly 形式紧随其后出现。

items.en: Modern English uses profoundly mainly as an intensifier of feelings, differences, and conditions such as deafness.
items.cn: 现代英语中，profoundly 主要用作情感、差异以及失聪等状况的强调语。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the profound family and the fundus root; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs and intensifiers of depth.
note.cn: 形近组围绕 profound 词族与 fundus 词根；近义组收其他表示「深、极其」的副词与强调语。

entries.definition: very deep or intense, or showing deep understanding
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深刻的、深远的、深奥的」，是 profoundly 的基础词。

entries.definition: the noun for depth of thought, feeling, or meaning
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「深刻、深奥、深沉」。

entries.definition: another noun for the quality of being profound
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「深刻、深奥」，由 profound 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: a wrongly spelled adverb that drops the o; the correct English form is profoundly
entries.definitionCN: 一种常见的错误拼写，漏掉了字母 o；正确拼写是 profoundly。

entries.definition: an adverb meaning to a great depth or degree; plainer and more frequent than profoundly
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「深深地、非常」，比 profoundly 更平实常用。

entries.definition: an adverb meaning with great force or feeling, with no image of depth
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「强烈地」，强调强度，不带「深」的意象。

entries.definition: an adverb meaning completely, used mostly with negatives and contrasts
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「完全地」，多与否定或对比搭配。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts pro- and fundus and the adjectives and verbs profoundly actually modifies.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语成分 pro- 与 fundus，以及 profoundly 实际修饰的形容词和动词。

normal.en: Pro plus fundus means down to the bottom; profoundly is the adverb of that depth.
normal.cn: pro 加 fundus 意为「一直到底」；profoundly 就是这种深度的副词形式。

normal.en: The family is tight: profound, profoundly, profundity, all from one Latin bottom word.
normal.cn: 这一词族很紧凑：profound、profoundly、profundity 都来自同一个表示「底」的拉丁词。

normal.en: Collocations show the main uses: profoundly affected, profoundly important, profoundly grateful.
normal.cn: 搭配显示主要用法：profoundly affected、profoundly important、profoundly grateful。

normal.en: In medicine, profoundly deaf is a standard term for very serious hearing loss.
normal.cn: 在医学上，profoundly deaf 是表示重度失聪的标准说法。

normal.en: Compare deeply: it is far more common in speech, while profoundly is stronger and more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 deeply：口语中 deeply 远比 profoundly 常用，profoundly 更强、更正式。

abstract.en: Drop a stone into a deep well and count the long seconds before the sound returns.
abstract.cn: 把一块石头投进深井，数一数声音回来之前那漫长的几秒。

abstract.en: Picture an iceberg: only the tip shows, while the huge mass stays below the surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一座冰山：只露出尖端，庞大的主体都藏在水面之下。

abstract.en: Think of a low voice that vibrates through the floor of the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一个低沉的声音透过房间的地板震动过来。

examples.en: The discovery profoundly changed how doctors treat the disease.
examples.cn: 这一发现彻底改变了医生治疗这种疾病的方法。

examples.en: She is profoundly grateful to the friends who helped her rebuild the house.
examples.cn: 她对帮助她重建房屋的朋友们深怀感激。

examples.en: The two accounts of the night are profoundly different.
examples.cn: 关于那一夜的两份记述截然不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若方的里」——一口深井的方底里，声音要很久才回来，可见深之极；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、向下）+ fundus（底部）→ profundus（深的、无底的）→ 古法语 profond → 英语 profound → 加 -ly 成 profoundly；核心义是「一直到底」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of profoundly all measure how far something goes down from the surface: into feeling and effect, into extent, into thought, and into the body.
sensesIntro.cn: profoundly 的四个义项都在衡量某物从表面向下延伸多远：向下进入情感与影响、进入程度、进入思想，以及进入身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into a deep well, with the echo arriving long after.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头被投进深井，回响很久以后才传来。

branches.en: FEELING: emotion and effect that reach all the way down.
branches.cn: 情感线：一直深达底部的感情与影响。

branches.en: EXTENT: depth used as a measure of how extreme a difference is.
branches.cn: 程度线：用深度衡量差异极端到什么地步。

branches.en: THOUGHT: insight described as having most of its mass below the surface.
branches.cn: 思想线：见地被描述为大部分重量藏在水面之下。

branches.en: BODY: sounds, sleep, and deafness described in literal space.
branches.cn: 身体线：声音、睡眠与失聪用字面意义上的空间来描述。

branches.en: Deep feeling and extreme degree are two readings of the same bottom image.
branches.cn: 深切的情感与极端的程度，是同一个「底部」意象的两种读法。

intro.en: Profoundly is Latin pro- plus fundus, plus the English adverb suffix -ly; the family also includes profundity and profoundness.
intro.cn: profoundly 由拉丁语 pro- 加 fundus，再加英语副词后缀 -ly 构成；同族还有 profundity 与 profoundness。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundus and profundus are recorded; fundus is also the source of English fund and fundament.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundus 与 profundus 均有文献记录；fundus 也是英语 fund 与 fundament 的来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把含义推向下方。

items.example: Fundus gives the bottom of the image.
items.exampleCN: fundus 提供意象的「底部」。

items.example: Profundus is the direct ancestor of profound.
items.exampleCN: profundus 是 profound 的直接前身。

items.example: Profound carries the Latin word into English.
items.exampleCN: profound 把拉丁词带入英语。

items.example: It forms profundity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 profundity。

items.example: It forms profoundness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 profoundness。

items.meaning: a supply of money, from Latin fundus
items.meaningCN: 资金；基金，来自拉丁语 fundus
items.example: Fund shares the bottom root.
items.exampleCN: fund 共享「底」这个词根。

items.example: Fundamental keeps the base image.
items.exampleCN: fundamental 保留了「基座」意象。

definition_zh: 大量的；丰富的；过多的；极其慷慨的
definition_en: existing or happening in very large amounts, often more than is needed
core_image: 水从桶沿不断溢出，桶外积成一滩
scene: 婚礼结束后，客人在门口道谢，说主人太慷慨了。After the wedding, the guests thanked their hosts for a profuse spread of food and drink at every table.
sceneCN: 这里 profuse 是「大量的、丰富的」（第 1 个义项：数量多得接近溢出）；句意：婚礼结束后，客人在门口道谢，说主人太慷慨了，每张桌子都摆满了丰盛的食物和饮料。

pos.zh: 极其慷慨的；毫不吝惜的

derivatives.zh: 由基础词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「大量；丰富；挥霍」
由基础词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「大量地；连声道」
加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「丰盛；挥霍」
较少见的同义形容词，义为「慷慨的；丰盛的」

senses.title: Existing in very large amounts
senses.definition: present or produced in very large quantities
senses.definitionCN: 以极大数量出现或产生的
senses.example: Profuse flowers covered the whole hillside.
senses.exampleCN: 漫山遍野开满了大量的花。
senses.why: The Latin verb fundere means to pour, and pro- means forth, so the core image is something poured out till it overflows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 fundere 意为「倾倒」，pro- 意为「向前、向外」，核心意象就是倒出来直到溢出，于是「大量、丰富」成为基本义。

senses.title: Given without restraint
senses.titleCN: 极其慷慨的；毫不吝惜的
senses.definition: giving or offered very generously, sometimes in a showy way
senses.definitionCN: 给予时出手极为大方，有时带点铺张意味
senses.example: Our hosts were profuse in their hospitality.
senses.exampleCN: 主人待客极为慷慨。
senses.why: If something is poured out without measure, the same image shifts from amount to the giving itself, hence lavish generosity.
senses.whyCN: 既然是毫无节制地倾倒，意象就从「量」移到「给予」这个动作上，于是产生「慷慨、不吝惜」的义项。

senses.title: Too much of a physical process
senses.definition: producing or losing a body fluid in unusually large quantity
senses.definitionCN: 身体液体以异常大的数量产生或流失
senses.example: The patient complained of profuse sweating at night.
senses.exampleCN: 病人诉说夜里大量出汗。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the pouring image literally, so a river of sweat or blood can be called profuse.
senses.whyCN: 医学沿用「往外涌」的字面画面，汗或血像水一样流出来，就可以说 profuse，这一义项常出现在医学语境。

senses.title: Abundant in ornament or display
senses.definition: so elaborate or full of detail that it looks excessive
senses.definitionCN: 装饰或细节繁复到显得过度的
senses.example: The hall was decorated with profuse gold embroidery.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅装饰着繁复的金色刺绣。
senses.why: Abundance seen through the eye becomes richness of ornament, and richness easily leans toward excess.
senses.whyCN: 从眼睛看去的「多」会变成装饰的繁复，而繁复又容易滑向「过度」，所以这一义项带有铺张色彩。

senses.title: Expressed in an emotional overflow
senses.definition: expressed so abundantly that the feeling seems to spill over
senses.definitionCN: 表达得极其多，情感像是漫溢出来
senses.example: She sent profuse apologies for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 她为延误一再道歉。
senses.why: Emotion is also something that can be poured, so profuse thanks or tears are the same overflow in a human form.
senses.whyCN: 情感同样可以被「倒」出来，因此连声的道谢或不停流的眼泪只是同一个「满溢」意象在人际层面上的表现。

intro.en: Profuse comes from Latin profusus, poured out, the past participle of profundere, from pro, forth, and fundere, to pour.
intro.cn: profuse 来自拉丁语 profusus（倒出来的），是 profundere 的过去分词，由 pro（向前）和 fundere（倾倒）构成。

items.en: Fundere means to pour, and pro- adds the sense of forth or forward.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾倒，pro- 加上「向前、往外」的意思。

items.en: Profundere means to pour out, and its participle profusus describes what has been poured.
items.cn: profundere 意为倒出，其分词 profusus 描述「已经倒出来的」东西。

items.en: Profusus also develops the moral sense of wastefully lavish or squandered.
items.cn: profusus 同时也发展出「挥霍的、浪费的」这一评价性含义。

items.en: The adjective enters English through French forms, meaning poured out, lavish, or abundant.
items.cn: 这个形容词经由法语形式进入英语，意为「倾倒的、慷慨的、丰富的」。

items.en: Writers apply the word to blood, sweat, tears, and rhetoric, spreading it beyond generosity.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的作者把它用于血、汗、泪与言辞，使它不再只表示慷慨。

items.en: Modern English keeps the medical sense of heavy bleeding or sweating alongside the general sense of abundance.
items.cn: 现代英语既保留「大量出血或出汗」的医学义，也保留一般的「丰富、大量」义。

note.en: Profuse sits in the Latin pour family, close to profusion and profusely, and beside amount words such as abundant and copious.
note.cn: profuse 属于拉丁语「倾倒」词族，与 profusion、profusely 同源，并与 abundant、copious 这类「量多」词相邻。

entries.definition: a very large amount of something
in large amounts
entries.definitionCN: 大量地；连声地（同根副词）

entries.definition: to mix up or fail to understand
entries.definitionCN: 混淆；使困惑；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: existing in large quantities
entries.definitionCN: 丰富的；充裕的（中性，褒义）

entries.definition: plentiful, especially of notes, tears, or words
entries.definitionCN: 大量的（书面语，多形容笔记、泪水、言辞）

entries.definition: more than is right or sensible

normalIntro.en: Profuse is the pour family: pro plus fundere, something poured out until it runs over.
normalIntro.cn: profuse 属于「倒」这个词族：pro 加 fundere，倒出来直到漫溢。

normal.en: Profuse apologies means apologising again and again.
normal.cn: profuse apologies 就是一而再地道歉。

normal.en: Profuse sweating describes a body losing water heavily.
normal.cn: profuse sweating 形容身体大量流失水分。

normal.en: Profusion is the noun of the same family, meaning great abundance.
normal.cn: profusion 是同一词族的名词，意为大量、丰富。

normal.en: Profusely is the adverb, as in thanked us profusely.
normal.cn: profusely 是副词，例如 thanked us profusely 意为连声道谢。

normal.en: Compare abundant: abundant is neutral and positive, profuse often hints at more than enough.
normal.cn: 对比 abundant：abundant 中性偏褒，profuse 常暗示「多到超过需要」。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket under a tap that nobody has turned off.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头开着没人关，水桶已经满了还在往外流。

abstract.en: Think of a host carrying another tray of food although every table is full.
abstract.cn: 想象主人端着又一大托盘菜走过来，而每张桌子都已摆满。

abstract.en: See a runner with sweat pouring down his face in the heat.
abstract.cn: 想象炎热中跑步的人，汗水顺着脸往下淌。

examples.en: The doctor noted profuse bleeding from the wound.
examples.cn: 医生注意到伤口大量出血。

examples.en: He offered profuse apologies for being late.
examples.cn: 他为迟到连连道歉。

examples.en: The orchard produced a profuse crop of pears this year.
examples.cn: 这片果园今年结出了大量梨子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼 弗 死」——水泼出去，怎么泼也泼不死，因为水太多了；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、向外）+ fundere（倾倒）→ profundere（倒出）→ profusus（已经倒出的）→ 英语 profuse，核心义「倒出来直到漫溢」。

sensesIntro.en: Profuse begins with sheer quantity, widens to generous giving, and then narrows into medical fluids, ornament, and emotional display.
sensesIntro.cn: profuse 首先表示纯粹的数量之多，扩展到慷慨给予，再收窄到医学上的体液、装饰的繁复与情感的宣泄。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water running over the rim of a full bucket.
core.cn: 核心意象：水从满桶的桶沿溢出来。

branches.en: Pure abundance is the basic quantity sense.
branches.cn: 单纯的「量大」是基本义项。

branches.en: Giving without measure is the generosity sense.
branches.cn: 毫无节制地给予是「慷慨」义项。

branches.en: Sweat and blood pouring out is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 汗和血往外涌是医学义项。

branches.en: A lavish host and a profuse harvest both show something poured out beyond need.
branches.cn: 铺张的主人与丰盛的收成，都体现「倒出来超出所需」。

branches.en: Ornament and apologies are abundance transferred to the eye and the voice.
branches.cn: 装饰与道歉是把「多」移到眼睛和声音上。

intro.en: Profuse is built from the Latin prefix pro- and the verb fundere, with English profusion, profusely, and profuseness around it.
intro.cn: profuse 由拉丁语前缀 pro- 与动词 fundere 构成，周围有英语的 profusion、profusely 与 profuseness。

latinIntro.en: Fundere means to pour, and pro- means forth, so profusus means poured out.
latinIntro.cn: fundere 意为倾倒，pro- 意为向前，profusus 即「倒出来的」。

items.example: The prefix pro- adds the outward direction.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 加入「向外」的方向。

items.example: Profusus is the participle behind the adjective.

definition_zh: 禁止性的；价格高得让人望而却步的；（法律上）禁止的
definition_en: so expensive that it prevents people from buying or doing something, or relating to a formal ban
core_image: 价签上写着买不起的数字，顾客在门口停下脚步
scene: 一对年轻夫妻站在学区房广告前，看了报价后摇头走开。The couple walked away from the advert because the rents in that district had become prohibitive.
sceneCN: 这里 prohibitive 是「贵得让人买不起」（第 1 个义项：价格高到阻止人购买）；句意：一对年轻夫妻站在学区房广告前，看了报价后摇头走开，因为那一带的租金已经高得让人望而却步。

pos.zh: 高得让人望而却步的；令人却步的
禁止性的；（法律上）禁止的

collocations.zh: 高得让人买不起的价格

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「禁止；阻止」
由基础词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「禁止；禁令」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「高得令人却步地」
由动词加过去分词构成，义为「被禁止的」
加施事后缀 -or 构成，较少见，义为「禁止者；禁令发布者」

senses.title: So costly that it blocks purchase
senses.titleCN: 价格高得让人买不起的
senses.definition: too expensive for most people, so that it stops them from buying or taking part
senses.definitionCN: 价格过高，使大多数人无法购买或参与
senses.example: The cost of a second car is prohibitive for many families.
senses.exampleCN: 对许多家庭来说，再买一辆车的开销高得令人却步。
senses.why: The Latin prefix pro- means before or in front, so something prohibitive stands in front of you as a barrier; a price can act as that barrier.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 pro- 意为「在前方」，prohibitive 的东西像一道挡在前面的墙；价格也能成为这样的障碍，于是「贵到买不起」由此而来。

senses.title: Formally banning by law or rule
senses.definition: relating to an official ban that forbids an action
senses.definitionCN: 与正式禁止某项行为的禁令相关的
senses.example: The council passed a prohibitive rule on water use in dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会通过了一项旱季用水禁令。
senses.why: This is the word at its most literal: the verb prohibit means to forbid, and the adjective names the nature of the ban itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的义项：动词 prohibit 就是「禁止」，形容词用来描述禁令本身的性质，所以表示「禁止性的」。

senses.title: Deterring by being too high
senses.titleCN: 高得令人却步的（税费、门槛等）
senses.definition: so high in tax, rent, or requirement that it stops people acting
senses.definitionCN: 税费、租金或门槛高到使人放弃行动
senses.example: Prohibitive import duties kept foreign goods off the shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 高得吓人的进口关税让外国货无法上架。
senses.why: A barrier need not be made of money itself; taxes and entry conditions can also stand in front of a market.
senses.whyCN: 障碍并不一定由价格本身构成，关税或准入门槛同样可以横在市场前面，所以「税费高到却步」是同一意象的扩展。

senses.title: Preventing by force of rule
senses.titleCN: 起阻止作用的；使人知难而退的
senses.definition: having the effect of discouraging or preventing an action, even without a formal ban
senses.definitionCN: 即使没有正式禁令，实际效果也是劝退或阻止
senses.example: The long application process proved prohibitive for most volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的申请流程让大多数志愿者知难而退。
senses.why: The image of a wall in front of the path moves from money to any practical obstacle that turns people away.
senses.whyCN: 挡在路前的墙这一意象，从金钱扩展为任何现实障碍：只要能把人劝退，都可以用 prohibitive 来形容。

senses.title: Technically forbidding rather than preventing
senses.titleCN: 禁止性的（与描述性相对）
senses.definition: worded as a ban rather than as a description or a recommendation
senses.definitionCN: 以禁令的方式表述，而非描述或建议
senses.example: The sign was prohibitive in tone rather than gentle.
senses.exampleCN: 这块标牌的语气是禁止性的，而不是温和的。
senses.why: Grammar and legal writing split bans from descriptions, so the word also labels the style of a rule.
senses.whyCN: 语法学和法律写作把「禁令式」与「描述式」区分开来，于是这个词也用来标注规定的语气类型。

intro.en: Prohibitive comes from the verb prohibit, from Latin prohibere, to hold back, a compound of pro, in front, and habere, to hold.
intro.cn: prohibitive 来自动词 prohibit，源于拉丁语 prohibere（拦住、阻止），由 pro（在前面）和 habere（握住）构成。

items.en: Habere means to hold, and pro- means in front, so prohibere pictures something held out to block a path.
items.cn: habere 意为握住，pro- 意为在前面，prohibere 的画面是伸出手臂挡住去路。

items.en: Prohibere develops the legal sense of forbidding or keeping away.
items.cn: prohibere 发展出「禁止、杜绝」的法律含义。

items.en: The adjective prohibitivus is formed on the participle prohibitus.
items.cn: 形容词 prohibitivus 由分词 prohibitus 派生而成。

items.en: The verb prohibit enters English by the fifteenth century, and the adjective prohibitive is first recorded in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 动词 prohibit 在十五世纪进入英语，形容词 prohibitive 首见于十六世纪。

items.en: Economists begin to speak of prohibitive duties, taxes so high they stop trade.
items.cn: 十八、十九世纪的经济学家开始说 prohibitive duties，即高到阻止贸易的关税。

items.en: Modern writers extend the price barrier sense to anything that deters by cost or effort.
items.cn: 现代作家把「价格障碍」推广到任何因代价或难度而使人却步的事物。

note.en: Prohibitive is the adjective of the forbid family, close to prohibit and prohibition, and beside cost words such as expensive and unaffordable.
note.cn: prohibitive 是「禁止」词族的形容词，与 prohibit、prohibition 同源，并与 expensive、unaffordable 这类「昂贵」词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Prohibitive comes from a hand held out to block the way: anything that stops you in your tracks.
normalIntro.cn: prohibitive 源于伸出的手挡住去路：凡是让你停下脚步的事，都能用这个词。

normal.en: Prohibitive cost is the most common pairing, as in the cost of housing.
normal.cn: prohibitive cost 是最常见的搭配，例如住房成本。

normal.en: Prohibitively expensive means the price itself is the barrier.
normal.cn: prohibitively expensive 意思是价格本身就是那道障碍。

normal.en: Prohibition is the noun of the same family, as in the prohibition of smoking.
normal.cn: prohibition 是同族名词，例如禁烟。

normal.en: Legal texts use prohibitive norms for rules that forbid rather than guide.
normal.cn: 法律文本用 prohibitive norms 指「禁止」而非「引导」的规范。

normal.en: Compare expensive: expensive simply means high in price, while prohibitive adds that the price keeps people away.
normal.cn: 对比 expensive：expensive 只说价格高，prohibitive 还强调价格把人挡在门外。

abstract.en: Picture a shopper reading the price tag and slowly putting the item back.
abstract.cn: 想象顾客看了价签，慢慢把商品放回货架。

abstract.en: Think of a gate with a printed rule nailed across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇大门上钉着一条明文规定，写着禁止通行。

abstract.en: See high customs duties as a wall around a harbour.
abstract.cn: 想象高高的关税像一堵墙，把港口围起来。

examples.en: The price of apartments in the city centre is prohibitive for young buyers.
examples.cn: 市中心公寓的价格对年轻买家来说高得令人却步。

examples.en: Solar panels were once prohibitively expensive for ordinary homes.
examples.cn: 太阳能电池板曾对普通家庭而言贵得离谱。

examples.en: The new law contains several prohibitive clauses about waste.
examples.cn: 这项新法包含若干关于废弃物的禁止性条款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑 若 喝 必备 体 无」——太贵了，扑过去想买也「喝」不上（买不起），干脆别买；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（在前面）+ habere（握住）→ prohibere（拦住；禁止）→ prohibitus → 英语 prohibit，再加后缀 -ive 得 prohibitive，核心义「挡在前面，使人过不去」。

sensesIntro.en: Prohibitive starts as the literal adjective of a legal ban, then moves to price and cost as a barrier, and finally to anything that deters by effort or rules.
sensesIntro.cn: prohibitive 首先表示法律禁令的性质，然后转指价格与成本构成的障碍，最后泛指任何因代价或规则而使人却步的因素。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out to stop you entering.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只伸出来的手拦在门口。

branches.en: A price that blocks purchase is the everyday economic sense.
branches.cn: 让人买不起的价格是日常经济义项。

branches.en: A formal ban is the literal legal sense.
branches.cn: 正式禁令是字面上的法律义项。

branches.en: Taxes and thresholds act as the barrier in trade.
branches.cn: 关税与门槛在贸易中充当障碍。

branches.en: Both a high price and a heavy duty keep ordinary people out of the market.
branches.cn: 高价与重税都把普通人挡在市场之外。

branches.en: The barrier can be practical effort or the grammar of a forbidding rule.
branches.cn: 障碍可以是现实的麻烦，也可以是禁令式的表述方式。

intro.en: Prohibitive is built on the Latin verb prohibere, with English prohibit, prohibition, and prohibited around it.
intro.cn: prohibitive 建立在拉丁语动词 prohibere 之上，周围有英语的 prohibit、prohibition 与 prohibited。

latinIntro.cn: prohibere 由 pro（在前面）与 habere（握住）组成，意为拦住、禁止。

definition_zh: 投影仪；放映机；规划者；（心理学）投射者
definition_en: a machine that throws light and an image onto a screen or wall
core_image: 一束光从镜头射向前方，把画面打在墙上
scene: 研讨室里关上了灯，老师把讲义投到白墙上。The teacher switched off the lights and asked us to adjust the projector before the slide show began.
sceneCN: 这里 projector 是「投影仪」（第 1 个义项：把影像投射到屏幕或墙上的设备）；句意：研讨室里关上了灯，老师把讲义投到白墙上，还让我们在幻灯片开始前把投影仪调好。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「投射；投影；规划」
由基础词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「投射；投影；预测」
复合名词，义为「投影镜头」
同根名词，义为「抛射物；炮弹」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可投射的；可预见的」

senses.title: A machine that throws an image
senses.definition: an optical device that projects an image or light onto a screen or wall
senses.definitionCN: 把影像或光投射到屏幕或墙上的光学设备
senses.example: The projector threw a map onto the white wall.
senses.exampleCN: 投影仪把一幅地图投到白墙上。
senses.why: The Latin prefix pro- means forward and iacere means to throw, so the core image is something thrown forward; a projector is the tool doing the throwing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 pro- 意为「向前」，iacere 意为「扔」，核心意象就是「往前抛出」；投影仪正是完成「抛」这个动作的工具。

senses.title: A person who plans
senses.definition: a person who plans or devises a scheme or undertaking
senses.definitionCN: 规划、设计某项计划或事业的人
senses.example: As the chief projector of the scheme, she wrote every proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 作为这项计划的主要筹划人，每份方案都由她来写。
senses.why: To project also means to throw a plan forward in time, so a projector became a word for the person who plans ahead.
senses.whyCN: project 还有「把计划投向未来」的意思，于是 projector 也曾被用来指提前谋划的人，这是今天较少见的旧用法。

senses.title: Something that thrusts forward
senses.definition: a device or body part that drives something out with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力把某物推出或射出的装置或身体部位
senses.example: The projector muscle of a frog forces water from its throat.
senses.exampleCN: 蛙的喷射肌把水从喉部推出去。
senses.why: The Latin participle projectus means thrust forward, so any device that drives something ahead can be called a projector.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词 projectus 意为「被向前推」，因此任何把东西往前推射的装置都可以叫 projector，这一义项偏技术性。

senses.title: A structure projecting from a surface
senses.definition: a part or structure that stands out from a larger surface
senses.definitionCN: 从较大表面伸出来的部件或结构
senses.example: The balcony is a simple projector of concrete from the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 阳台是从墙面上伸出去的一块混凝土。
senses.why: If something is thrown forward, it sticks out; architecture borrows this sense for parts that jut from a building.
senses.whyCN: 被「抛向前方」的东西会凸出来，建筑学借用这一层意思，指从楼体探出的构件。

senses.title: A person who projects feelings
senses.definition: in psychology, a person who attributes their own feelings to others
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中把自己的感受归于他人的人
senses.example: The analyst described her as a projector of her own anger.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师把她称为把自己愤怒投射出去的人。
senses.why: In psychology the image is turned inward: feelings are thrown onto other people, and the one who throws them is the projector.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这束光转向内心：情感被抛到别人身上，完成这个抛掷的人就被称作 projector。

intro.en: Projector comes from Latin projector, one who throws forth, from proicere, to throw forward, built on pro, forward, and iacere, to throw.
intro.cn: projector 来自拉丁语 projector（向前抛出的人），源于 proicere（向前扔），由 pro（向前）与 iacere（扔）构成。

items.en: Iacere means to throw, and pro- adds the direction forward.
items.cn: iacere 意为扔，pro- 加上「向前」的方向。

items.en: Proicere means to throw forward, and its participle projectus describes something thrust out.
items.cn: proicere 意为向前抛出，其分词 projectus 描述被推出的东西。

items.en: Projector first names a person who forms a plan, and later a schemer.
items.cn: projector 最初指制定计划的人，后来也指「策划者、阴谋家」。

items.en: Optical use appears with magic lanterns, devices that threw light and pictures onto a screen.
items.cn: 随着「幻灯机」出现，这个词有了光学用法，即把光和图像投到屏幕上。

items.en: Film, slide, and overhead projectors spread the device sense into classrooms and cinemas.
items.cn: 电影、幻灯片与高架投影仪把「设备」义带进教室和影院。

items.en: Modern English adds digital and pocket projectors, while the planning sense becomes rare.
items.cn: 现代英语又有数字投影仪和便携投影仪，而「规划者」义项已少见。

note.en: Projector belongs to the Latin throw family of project and projection, and sits beside screen and display words.
note.cn: projector 属于拉丁语「抛」词族，与 project、projection 同源，并与 screen、display 这类显示词相邻。

normal.en: Project a film means to throw it onto a screen.

normal.en: A film projector is the older cinema machine.
normal.cn: film projector 是较早的电影放映机。
